items.objective: Explain scarcity, constraints and why choices involve trade-offs. Identify the alternatives forgone in a decision.
items.title: Scarcity & trade-offs / 稀缺與取捨
items.en: Scarcity means available resources cannot satisfy every want. A constraint limits feasible choices. Choosing one use of time or money gives up other possible uses.
items.zh: 稀缺同時涉及有限資源和人們的需要。預算、時間和能力限制可行選項；做選擇就要放棄其他用途。
items.example: Example 例：You have 2 hours; studying takes 2 hours and working takes 2 hours. You can do either, but cannot do both. 只有兩小時，讀書和打工各要兩小時，兩者不能同時完成。
items.question: You have $100; two activities each cost $80. What creates the trade-off? 兩項活動各要 $80，取捨來自什麼？
options: Limited budget / 預算有限
No preferences / 沒有喜好
Unlimited resources / 資源無限
No alternatives / 沒有選項
items.why: The budget prevents choosing both. 預算限制使你必須取捨。

items.objective: Calculate the opportunity cost of an action, including money spent and the value of the **best** forgone alternative. Avoid adding the values of several mutually exclusive alternatives together.
items.title: Opportunity cost / 機會成本
items.en: Count the resources actually sacrificed plus the value of the best forgone alternative. When alternatives are mutually exclusive, their values are not added together. Avoid counting the same cost twice.
items.zh: 機會成本包括實際犧牲的金錢與最佳放棄選項的價值。互斥選項只取最佳一個，避免重複計算。
items.example: Example 例：A free study session replaces a $200 job or a free outing worth $120. Opportunity cost = max(200,120) = $200. 免費讀書活動的最佳替代方案是賺 $200。
items.question: A $50 concert replaces a job earning $100 or a free walk worth $30. Opportunity cost? $50 演唱會取代賺 $100 的工作或價值 $30 的散步，成本多少？
items.why: $50 ticket plus $100 best alternative = $150. 門票加最佳放棄收入，散步不另加。

items.objective: Compare alternatives using benefits and opportunity costs, including benefits that are not naturally expressed in dollars: ask what someone would be willing to pay for them.
items.title: Valuing alternatives / 比較方案價值
items.en: Put benefits and costs on a common scale using willingness to pay. Compare the net benefit of each feasible option, including time and forgone income. A benefit can have economic value without being cash income.
items.zh: 可用願付價格衡量快樂或休息等非金錢收益。把每個方案的收益減去相關成本，並包括放棄收入，再比較淨收益。
items.example: Example 例：A trip brings enjoyment valued at $500, costs $200 and replaces $150 work. Net advantage over work = 500−200−150 = $150. 旅遊的額外淨收益為 $150。
items.question: Enjoyment is worth $300; ticket costs $100; forgone wages are $250. Net advantage of attending? 參加活動的淨優勢？
items.why: 300−100−250 = −50. Attending gives less value than the work alternative.

items.objective: Recognize a sunk cost and exclude it from a forward-looking decision; compare the **additional** benefit and **additional** cost of proceeding.
items.title: Sunk cost / 沉沒成本
items.en: An unrecoverable past cost cannot change with today's decision. Compare the future benefit and future cost of continuing; include any recoverable resale value that would be sacrificed.
items.zh: 無法收回的過去支出不隨今天的選擇改變。繼續與否只比較未來相關成本及收益；若可出售資產，放棄的售價仍有關。
items.example: Example 例：Already spent $5m; finishing costs $1m and yields $3m. Continue because 3−1 = +$2m. 已花 $5m 不影響現在完成的額外淨收益。
items.question: Past research cost $8m; completion costs $2m; new revenue $1.5m. What should the firm do? 應否完成？
options: Continue; past cost is large / 繼續
Stop only if past cost is zero / 過去成本零才停止
Continue; revenue is positive / 繼續
Stop; future net benefit is negative / 停止
items.why: 1.5−2 = −$0.5m. Continuing reduces wealth further. 繼續會額外損失 $0.5m。

items.objective: Apply marginal reasoning: take an additional action when its marginal benefit exceeds its marginal cost, and identify the relevant margin in a numerical question.
items.title: Marginal reasoning / 邊際決策
items.en: Marginal means additional. Take the next unit when its extra benefit exceeds its extra cost. Total or average benefits cannot by themselves determine whether one more unit is worthwhile.
items.zh: 邊際是額外一單位的變化。下一單位的收益高於成本就值得；總收益或平均收益不足以決定是否多做一單位。
items.example: Example 例：A third study hour adds 8 expected marks and costs leisure valued at 5 mark-equivalents. Extra net gain = 3, so study that hour. 第三小時額外淨收益為 3。
items.question: An extra unit brings $12 revenue and $15 additional cost. Should output increase? 多做一件是否值得？
options: No; marginal net benefit is −$3 / 不值得
No; all production is unprofitable / 全部停產
Yes; total sales rise / 值得
Yes; average cost may fall / 值得
items.why: 12−15 = −3 for this additional unit; this does not establish the profitability of all output.

items.objective: Predict how a change in rewards, penalties or other incentives changes behavior.
items.title: Incentives / 激勵
items.en: A reward or penalty changes the relative payoff from an action. Predict the response at the affected margin, allowing for unintended consequences and differences between individuals.
items.zh: 獎勵與懲罰會改變行動的相對收益。要辨認哪個選擇的成本或收益改變，並考慮行為反應及非預期效果。
items.example: Example 例：A charge on plastic bags raises the cost of using each bag, encouraging shoppers to bring reusable bags. 膠袋費改變每次使用膠袋的成本。
items.question: A parking fine increases, with enforcement unchanged. What incentive changes? 執法不變但罰款增加，誘因如何變？
options: The expected penalty falls / 預期罰則下降
Illegal parking becomes more costly / 違泊成本上升
Legal parking becomes prohibited / 合法泊車被禁
All drivers stop driving / 所有人停駕
items.why: A larger fine raises the expected cost of a violation, holding detection probability fixed.

items.objective: Explain how specialization and voluntary trade can benefit participants.
items.title: Specialization & exchange / 專門化與交換
items.en: Specialization lets people concentrate on activities with lower relative opportunity cost. Voluntary exchange can then give both a more valuable consumption bundle. Gains depend on the trade terms and available alternatives.
items.zh: 專門化讓人集中於機會成本較低的活動。適當交易條件下，雙方都可得到比自行生產更好的消費組合。
items.example: Example 例：A gives up 2 meals to make a shirt; B gives up 4. A sells a shirt for 3 meals: A gains 1 meal and B saves 1 meal. 一件衫換三餐令雙方獲益。
items.question: A's cost of a shirt is 2 meals; B's is 4. Which trade price benefits both strictly? 何種價格令雙方嚴格得益？
options: 1 meal / 一餐
2 meals / 兩餐
3 meals / 三餐
5 meals / 五餐
items.why: The price lies between 2 and 4. 價格介乎雙方機會成本之間。

items.objective: Define a market, market economy, property rights, and the “invisible hand”; explain how prices coordinate buyers' and sellers' choices.
items.title: Markets, prices & property / 市場、價格與產權
items.en: A market is a group of buyers and sellers. In a market economy, decentralized choices coordinate through prices. Property rights support ownership and exchange; the invisible hand describes how self-interested choices can coordinate resource allocation under suitable conditions.
items.zh: 市場是買家與賣家的集合；市場經濟靠分散決策及價格協調資源。產權保障擁有和交易權利，價格傳遞稀缺與價值資訊。
items.example: Example 例：Coffee becomes scarce; a higher price encourages conservation and greater supply. Enforceable ownership lets sellers receive payment. 咖啡價格上升同時影響買賣雙方誘因。
items.question: Which signal coordinates buyers and sellers in a market economy? 什麼訊號協調市場？
options: A fixed production order for every firm / 統一產量命令
Equal incomes for all / 所有人同收入
The disappearance of property rights / 取消產權
A common price / 市場價格
items.why: Prices communicate relative scarcity and incentives. 價格把稀缺資訊傳給市場參與者。

items.objective: Distinguish efficiency from equality and identify the potential trade-off between them.
items.title: Efficiency & equality / 效率與平等
items.en: Efficiency concerns the size of total economic benefits from resources. Equality concerns their distribution. Redistribution may improve equality while changing incentives and the total surplus; the trade-off depends on the policy.
items.zh: 效率問總收益是否最大；平等問收益如何分配。重新分配可能改善分配，同時改變工作或投資誘因。
items.example: Example 例：A tax-transfer policy gives poorer households more income, but may reduce the reward to extra work. 轉移支付改善分配，也可能影響工作誘因。
items.question: A policy redistributes income while reducing total surplus. Which description fits? 重分配同時減少總剩餘？
options: Equality may improve, efficiency falls / 平等可能改善，效率下降
Both must improve / 兩者必改善
Efficiency rises by definition / 效率必升
Neither distribution nor incentives changes / 均無變
items.why: Distribution and total gains are separate criteria. 分配與總收益須分別判斷。

items.objective: Recognize externalities and market power as possible sources of market failure; identify whether an intervention is motivated by efficiency, equality or both.
items.title: Market failure / 市場失靈
items.en: Externalities affect people outside a transaction; market power lets a participant influence price. Both can prevent efficient allocation. A policy may instead be motivated by equality, or pursue both aims.
items.zh: 外部性影響交易以外的人；市場力量讓參與者影響價格。兩者可使市場結果偏離效率；其他政策可能主要關心收入分配。
items.example: Example 例：A smoke restriction protects bystanders, addressing an externality. Food vouchers target low incomes, mainly addressing equality. 禁煙與食物券的政策動機不同。
items.question: A rule reduces pollution imposed on nearby residents. Its direct efficiency rationale? 減少居民承受污染的效率理由？
options: Increasing market power / 增加市場力量
Correcting an externality / 修正外部性
Eliminating every trade-off / 消除所有取捨
Guaranteeing equal profit / 保證同利潤
items.why: The rule addresses costs borne by nonparticipants. 污染成本由交易外的第三方承受。

items.objective: Explain the role of assumptions, simplified models, observations and evidence in economic analysis.
items.title: Models & evidence / 模型與證據
items.en: Models deliberately omit detail to isolate important relationships. Assumptions should fit the question and time horizon. Observations generate hypotheses, and evidence can support or challenge them.
items.zh: 模型透過假設省略細節，突出重要關係。假設應配合問題及時間範圍，理論須接受資料檢驗。
items.example: Example 例：A two-good economy isolates a production trade-off. Adding many goods may obscure this lesson without changing it. 兩商品模型令取捨更清楚。
items.question: Why use a simplified model? 為何簡化模型？
options: To avoid evidence / 避免資料
To include every detail / 包括所有細節
To isolate relevant mechanisms / 突出相關機制
To guarantee all predictions / 保證預測
items.why: Useful simplification focuses attention while retaining relevant relationships.

items.objective: Distinguish microeconomics from macroeconomics, and positive statements that can be tested from normative judgments about what ought to happen.
items.title: Micro, macro & statements / 微觀、宏觀與陳述
items.en: Microeconomics studies individual choices and markets; macroeconomics studies aggregate outcomes. Positive claims can be tested against evidence; normative claims include a value judgment about what ought to happen.
items.zh: 微觀研究個人及市場，宏觀研究整體經濟。實證陳述原則上可檢驗；規範陳述涉及應該如何做的價值觀。
items.example: Example 例：“A tax reduces purchases” is positive; “The government should impose it” is normative. 稅是否減少購買可測試，應否徵稅含價值判斷。
items.question: Which is normative? 哪句是規範陳述？
options: Higher costs reduced supply / 成本升令供給減少
Unemployment increased / 失業增加
Demand fell / 需求下降
Government should cut tax / 政府應減稅
items.why: “Should” expresses a recommendation requiring values as well as facts.

items.objective: Explain why economists may disagree about evidence, model assumptions, parameter estimates or values.
items.title: Why economists disagree / 經濟學家為何分歧
items.en: Economists can disagree about causal theories, assumptions, estimated responses or social values. Agreement on an effect does not guarantee agreement on whether a policy is desirable.
items.zh: 分歧可來自理論、假設、估計參數或價值觀。即使同意政策效果，也可能因對平等或效率的重視不同而不同意政策。
items.example: Example 例：Two economists agree a tax raises revenue, but disagree on how much labor supply falls and how important redistribution is. 對反應大小和分配價值均可有分歧。
items.question: Both agree on a policy's effects but prefer different outcomes. Main source of disagreement? 效果相同、偏好結果不同，分歧主要來自？
options: Values / 價值觀
Arithmetic error necessarily / 必定算錯
Different observed prices necessarily / 必定價格不同
No economic reasoning / 沒有經濟推理
items.why: Different normative weights can produce different recommendations.

items.objective: Read the circular-flow diagram: households own and sell factors of production and buy goods; firms buy factors and sell goods. Trace the corresponding flows of goods, inputs and money.
items.title: Circular flow / 經濟循環
items.en: Households supply factors to firms and buy goods from firms. Firms pay factor incomes and receive sales revenue. Real goods and inputs flow in the opposite direction to the associated money payments.
items.zh: 家庭提供勞工、土地及資本，並購買商品；企業購買要素並出售商品。實物流向與相應付款方向相反。
items.example: Example 例：You work in a bakery and receive wages through the factor market; buying bread uses the goods market. 你在餅店工作和買麵包屬不同市場。
items.question: In the factor market, households are usually what? 家庭在生產要素市場扮演什麼角色？
options: Sellers of all final goods / 所有成品賣家
Sellers of inputs / 要素賣家
Buyers of final bread / 麵包買家
Only government agents / 政府代理
items.why: Households own factors and supply them to firms. 家庭擁有並提供生產要素。

items.objective: Identify feasible, infeasible, efficient and inefficient points; explain why a point inside the frontier indicates unused or misallocated resources.
items.title: PPF locations / PPF 位置判讀
items.en: Points on the PPF are productively efficient; points inside are feasible but inefficient. Points outside are infeasible with current resources and technology. Moving from an interior point toward the frontier can increase output without sacrificing the other good.
items.zh: 邊界上具生產效率，內部可行但有資源閒置或分配不當，外部在現有條件下不可達。由內部改善可同時增加產量。
items.example: Example 例：With X+Y≤10, (4,4) is interior, (4,6) is on the frontier, and (6,6) is outside. 三點分別代表無效率、效率、不可行。
items.question: If X+Y≤10, how is (3,5) classified? 如何分類？
options: Infeasible / 不可行
Only feasible after trade / 交易後才可行
Feasible and inefficient / 可行但無效率
Feasible and efficient / 可行有效率
items.why: 3+5=8 leaves unused production capacity. 尚未用盡生產能力。

items.objective: Calculate the opportunity cost of one good in units of the other from a table or a PPF's slope. Interpret its magnitude and units.
items.title: PPF opportunity cost / PPF 機會成本
items.en: The opportunity cost of one extra X is Y sacrificed divided by additional X. With Y on the vertical axis, it is the magnitude of the PPF slope. Always state units.
items.zh: 每多一單位 X 的機會成本是放棄的 Y 除以增加的 X。Y 在縱軸時，這是斜率的絕對值；答案要寫商品單位。
items.example: Example 例：From (2,10) to (4,4), ΔX=2 and Y lost=6. Cost of 1 X=3 Y. 每單位 X 放棄三單位 Y。
items.question: Moving from (X=1,Y=12) to (X=3,Y=8), cost per extra X? 每單位 X 成本？
options: 4 Y
6 Y
2 Y
items.why: Four Y are sacrificed for two X, so 4/2=2 Y per X.

items.objective: Explain a straight-line PPF with constant opportunity cost and a bowed-out PPF with increasing opportunity cost due to resources differing in suitability.
items.title: PPF shape / PPF 形狀
items.en: A straight PPF has constant opportunity cost. A bowed-out PPF becomes steeper as more X is produced because resources transferred into X become less suitable for it relative to Y.
items.zh: 直線 PPF 代表固定機會成本；向外彎曲的 PPF 隨 X 增加而變陡，因資源專長不同，後來轉入 X 的資源代價較高。
items.example: Example 例：A specialist farmer switches first to farming; moving a skilled engineer into farming later may sacrifice much more engineering output. 依專長順序轉移資源，邊際代價會增加。
items.question: A bowed-out PPF normally implies what as X production expands? X 生產增加時通常怎樣？
options: Increasing cost in Y per X / 每 X 放棄更多 Y
Zero opportunity cost / 零成本
Constant cost everywhere / 各處成本固定
Unlimited output / 產量無限
items.why: Resources differ in suitability, producing increasing opportunity cost.

items.objective: Trace movements along the PPF versus shifts in the frontier. Show how a change in resources or good-specific technology affects production possibilities.
items.title: Moving versus shifting a PPF / 沿線與移線
items.en: A movement along the frontier reallocates existing resources. More resources or better technology can shift it outward. A technology improvement limited to X may raise its intercept while leaving the maximum Y unchanged.
items.zh: 沿 PPF 移動是既有資源重新分配；資源增加或技術進步令邊界外移。若只改善 X 技術，最大 Y 未必改變。
items.example: Example 例：Better computer technology raises possible computer output at many allocations; choosing more computers on the old frontier is simply reallocation. 技術進步與重新分配不同。
items.question: Only X technology improves. What may happen? 只有 X 技術改善？
options: All interior points become infeasible / 內部均不可行
X intercept rises; Y intercept can stay / X 截距升，Y 可不變
Both intercepts must fall / 均下降
Only a movement on old PPF / 只沿舊線移動
items.why: A good-specific technology change expands its production possibilities.

items.objective: Construct or interpret an economy-wide PPF from workers with different productivities, allocating production in order of comparative advantage; recognize inefficient allocations within the frontier.
items.title: Economy-wide PPF / 整體 PPF
items.en: Allocate each good first to workers with the lowest opportunity cost. As different workers switch activity, the aggregate PPF can have kinks. Producing inside that boundary can reflect inefficient assignment, even if everyone is busy.
items.zh: 先安排機會成本最低的人做相應商品。不同工人依次轉換活動，整體邊界可有折點；人人忙碌仍可能因分工不當而無效率。
items.example: Example 例：A makes 10 X or 20 Y; B makes 6 X or 6 Y. Starting from all Y, move B to X first: it sacrifices 1 Y per X, versus A's 2. 先轉 B 的代價較低。
items.question: From all-Y production, who should switch to X first in the example? 誰應先轉做 X？
options: The choice never matters / 永不影響
A / 甲
B / 乙
Both must switch together / 必須同時
items.why: B has the lower opportunity cost of X.

items.objective: Compare the gains in one good from giving up a given quantity of another at different locations on a bowed frontier.
items.title: Peace dividend on a bowed PPF / 彎曲 PPF 的轉產收益
items.en: On a bowed PPF, the opportunity cost of the horizontal good is greater where much of it is already produced. Giving up the same amount of that good can therefore release different quantities of the other good at different locations.
items.zh: 向外彎曲邊界上，已大量生產橫軸商品時，其邊際機會成本較高。因此在不同起點放棄同量該商品，可換回不同數量另一商品。
items.example: Example 例：With guns on X, shifting 1 unit away from guns near the high-guns end releases more butter than near the low-guns end. 在高軍備端減少一單位軍備可增加較多奶油。
items.question: Same small cut in guns on a bowed PPF: where is the butter gain generally larger? 同量減軍備，哪處奶油收益較大？
options: Low-guns end / 低軍備端
Always identical / 必相同
Always zero / 必為零
High-guns end / 高軍備端
items.why: The PPF is steeper at the high-guns end. 高軍備端斜率絕對值較大。

items.objective: Read axes, coordinates, intercepts and slope (`Δy/Δx`), including negative, zero and vertical slopes; distinguish a movement along a curve from a shift.
items.title: Axes, slope and shifts / 座標、斜率與移動
items.en: Read the axis labels before interpreting a graph. Slope is Δy/Δx; horizontal lines have zero slope and vertical slopes are undefined. A changed variable on an axis usually moves a point along a fixed relationship; another determinant can shift it.
items.zh: 先辨認橫縱軸及單位。斜率是縱向變化除橫向變化；水平為零，垂直斜率未定義。軸上的變數改變與整條關係移動須分清。
items.example: Example 例：From (Q=2,P=8) to (Q=6,P=4), slope=(4−8)/(6−2)=−1 dollars per unit. 斜率為每單位數量負一元。
items.question: From (x=1,y=7) to (x=4,y=1), slope? 斜率多少？

items.objective: Explain why correlation alone does not establish causation; recognize omitted variables and reverse causality in examples.
items.title: Correlation & causation / 相關與因果
items.en: A correlation can reflect a causal effect, an omitted common cause or reverse causality. A graph alone generally cannot distinguish these explanations. Ask what variable is missing and which direction of influence is plausible.
items.zh: 相關可能來自因果、共同遺漏因素或反向因果。單看圖形通常無法分辨；要問是否漏了因素，或因果方向倒轉。
items.example: Example 例：Cities with more crime hire more police. A positive police–crime correlation need not mean police cause crime. 高犯罪可引致增聘警察。
items.question: More lighters correlate with cancer; smoking is unmeasured. Main concern? 打火機與癌症相關但未量度吸煙？
options: A guaranteed random experiment / 隨機實驗
Omitted variable / 遺漏變數
Proof lighters cause cancer / 已證明因果
A normative statement / 規範陳述
items.why: Smoking can increase both lighter ownership and cancer risk.

title: Chapter 3 — Interdependence and the Gains from Trade

items.objective: Determine absolute advantage from output per unit of input or inputs needed per unit of output.
items.title: Absolute advantage / 絕對優勢
items.en: Compare output for the same input, or input needed for the same output. The producer making more per hour, or requiring fewer hours per unit, has absolute advantage in that good.
items.zh: 同投入比較產量，或同產量比較投入。每小時產量較高或每件所需時間較少的一方有絕對優勢。
items.example: Example 例：A makes 8 shirts per hour; B makes 5. A has absolute advantage in shirts. 每小時八件高於五件。
items.question: A needs 2 hours per table; B needs 3. Who has absolute advantage? 誰有絕對優勢？
options: Both equally / 相同
Cannot compare / 無法比較
A
B
items.why: A uses fewer hours per table.

items.objective: Calculate each producer's opportunity cost using either productivity data or time required. Express each answer in units of the other good, and use reciprocal costs consistently.
items.title: Opportunity-cost ratios / 機會成本比率
items.en: For output-per-period data, cost of X in Y equals maximum Y divided by maximum X. For time-per-unit data, divide time for X by time for Y. The reverse opportunity cost is its reciprocal.
items.zh: 若資料是同期間產量，X 的成本為最大 Y 除最大 X；若資料是每件時間，則為製作 X 時間除製作 Y 時間。兩種商品的成本互為倒數。
items.example: Example 例：One pizza takes 2 hours and one drink takes 1 hour. A pizza costs 2 drinks; one drink costs 0.5 pizza. 比率互為倒數。
items.question: A can make 12 X or 4 Y daily. Opportunity cost of 1 Y? 每 Y 成本？
options: 4 X
2 X
3 X
items.why: One Y uses a quarter of the day and sacrifices 3 X.

items.objective: Identify comparative advantage as the lower opportunity cost. Recognize that a producer can have absolute advantage in both goods and that trade can still create gains when opportunity costs differ.
items.title: Comparative advantage / 比較優勢
items.en: Comparative advantage belongs to the lower opportunity-cost producer. Even a producer with absolute advantage in both goods can gain from trade with someone whose relative costs differ. With two goods, one producer cannot have a strictly lower relative cost in both.
items.zh: 比較優勢看較低機會成本。即使一方兩種商品產能均較高，只要相對成本不同仍可互利交易；兩商品成本互為倒數，不能同時在兩者均有嚴格比較優勢。
items.example: Example 例：A makes 10 X or 20 Y; B makes 6 X or 6 Y. X costs A 2 Y and B 1 Y, so B has comparative advantage in X. B 的 X 相對成本較低。
items.question: Who has comparative advantage in Y in this example? 誰在 Y 有比較優勢？
options: A
B
Neither because A is faster at both / A 均較快所以沒有
Both strictly / 兩者均嚴格有
items.why: A gives up 0.5 X per Y; B gives up 1 X.

items.objective: Determine each producer's efficient specialization and exports. Construct the combined PPF by assigning production to those with the lowest opportunity cost first.
items.title: Specialization & combined PPF / 分工與整體 PPF
items.en: Assign extra production first to the lowest opportunity-cost producer. Each exports the good with comparative advantage. Combining their production possibilities can generate a kink where the first producer becomes fully specialized.
items.zh: 增加某商品時先用機會成本最低的生產者。各方出口有比較優勢的商品；當第一位已完全專門化，再轉第二位，整體 PPF 斜率改變。
items.example: Example 例：A: 10 X or 20 Y; B: 6 X or 6 Y. Both all-Y gives (0,26); B switches fully to X gives (6,20); both all-X gives (16,0). 邊界依次經過三點。
items.question: In this example, the efficient specialized output with A all-Y and B all-X is? 分工後產量？
items.why: Add A's 20 Y and B's 6 X.

items.objective: Find a mutually beneficial range for the price of a good in terms of the other good: it must lie strictly between the two producers' opportunity costs for both to gain from that exchange.
items.title: Terms of trade / 貿易條件
items.en: For both to gain strictly, the exchange price of a good must lie between their opportunity costs, expressed in the same units. At an endpoint, one party is indifferent in the simple constant-cost model.
items.zh: 雙方嚴格得益的價格須介乎兩者機會成本，單位必須一致。在端點時，其中一方只是無差異。
items.example: Example 例：X costs its exporter 1 Y and importer 2 Y. Trading 1 X for 1.5 Y benefits both. 出口者收多於成本，進口者付少於自製代價。
items.question: Costs of 1 X are 2 Y and 5 Y. Which price gives strict gains to both? 哪個價格互利？
options: 1 Y
2 Y
3 Y
6 Y
items.why: 3 lies strictly between 2 and 5.

items.objective: Use production and trade quantities to calculate consumption after trade, and compare each person's consumption with their no-trade possibilities.
items.title: Consumption after trade / 交易後消費
items.en: For each good, consumption equals production minus exports plus imports. Compare the resulting bundle with what the producer could make alone, or calculate the resources it would require without trade.
items.zh: 每種商品的消費等於產量減出口加進口。比較交易後組合與個人原本生產能力，可判斷是否獲益。
items.example: Example 例：B produces 6 X and exports 2 X for 3 Y; B consumes (4 X,3 Y). Its own PPF X+Y=6 cannot produce this total of 7. B 可消費超出原邊界的組合。
items.question: Produce 10 X, export 3 X and import 6 Y. Consumption? 生產十 X，出口三 X，進口六 Y？
items.why: Subtract exports and add imports good by good.

items.objective: Recognize that trade can allow consumption beyond an individual producer's own PPF; aggregate production still uses available resources and technology.
items.title: Production versus consumption / 生產與消費
items.en: Trade changes consumption possibilities without automatically changing production technology. Individual consumption can lie outside an individual's PPF, while economy-wide production remains feasible and total consumption respects total available goods.
items.zh: 交易擴大個人可消費組合，但不會自動改變技術。個人消費可在自己的 PPF 外，整體生產仍受資源限制。
items.example: Example 例：A trades part of its specialized output for B's good. A consumes a mix it cannot efficiently produce alone, while aggregate goods still equal production. 交換重新分配既有商品。
items.question: A consumes outside its own PPF after trade. What follows? 交易後消費在個人 PPF 外，代表什麼？
options: Trade expanded consumption opportunities / 貿易擴大消費選擇
Its technology must have improved / 技術必改善
World production is infeasible / 世界生產不可行
Scarcity disappeared / 稀缺消失
items.why: A consumption gain does not require a technological shift.

items.objective: Analyze how a productivity change can alter comparative advantage and potential trade patterns. If both producers have identical opportunity-cost ratios, this simple two-good model has no comparative-advantage gain from specialization.
items.title: Productivity changes & trade / 生產力變化與貿易
items.en: Recalculate opportunity costs after productivity changes; absolute output growth alone does not determine trade patterns. Equal opportunity-cost ratios remove comparative-advantage gains in the simple two-good model.
items.zh: 生產力改變後要重算相對成本；只看產量上升不足以判斷貿易方向。兩方機會成本相同時，簡化模型沒有比較優勢收益。
items.example: Example 例：A makes 10 X or 20 Y; B improves from 6 X or 6 Y to 6 X or 12 Y. Both now give up 2 Y per X. B 的改善令相對成本一致。
items.question: Both countries now sacrifice 3 Y per X. In the simple model, what happens to comparative-advantage gains? 相對成本相同時？
options: Both export X necessarily / 必均出口 X
They disappear / 消失
They must double / 必加倍
Only the bigger country gains / 只大國得益
items.why: Equal relative costs leave no mutually advantageous price interval.

title: Chapter 4 — The Market Forces of Supply and Demand

items.objective: Define quantity demanded and quantity supplied; explain the laws of demand and supply, holding other influences constant.
items.title: Demand and supply laws / 供需法則
items.en: Quantity demanded is how much buyers are willing and able to buy at a given price; quantity supplied is what sellers are willing and able to sell. Holding other factors constant, higher price lowers Qd and raises Qs.
items.zh: 需求量是買家在某價願意及能夠購買的數量；供給量是賣家願意及能夠出售的數量。其他因素不變時，價格升令 Qd 降、Qs 升。
items.example: Example 例：At $5 buyers want 20 units; at $6 they want 16. This is a downward relationship between price and quantity demanded. 價格上升令需求量下降。
items.question: Holding other factors fixed, a higher price usually does what? 其他不變，價格上升？
options: Shifts both curves right / 均右移
Makes both quantities zero / 均歸零
Lowers Qd and raises Qs / Qd 降、Qs 升
Raises Qd and lowers Qs / Qd 升、Qs 降
items.why: This combines the laws of demand and supply.

items.objective: Distinguish a change in a good's own price, which moves along its curve, from a change in another determinant, which shifts the curve.
items.title: Movement or shift / 沿線或移線
items.en: A good's own price moves the quantity along its existing demand or supply curve. A change in another determinant, such as income or input cost, shifts the relevant curve. State clearly which market is being studied.
items.zh: 本商品自身價格改變令數量沿現有曲線移動；收入、投入成本等其他因素改變才移動曲線。先確定分析哪一個市場。
items.example: Example 例：Coffee gets cheaper: move along coffee demand. Tea gets more expensive: coffee demand may shift right because tea is a substitute. 咖啡和茶價格對咖啡市場影響不同。
items.question: Coffee's own price falls. What happens to its demand curve, other things equal? 咖啡本身價格下降？
options: Shift demand right / 需求右移
Shift demand left / 需求左移
Shift supply left / 供給左移
Move along the curve / 沿曲線移動
items.why: Own-price changes affect quantity demanded along a fixed curve.

items.objective: Predict demand shifts caused by income (normal versus inferior goods), related goods (substitutes versus complements), tastes, expectations and the number of buyers.
items.title: Demand determinants / 需求因素
items.en: Income raises demand for normal goods and lowers demand for inferior goods. A substitute's higher price raises own demand; a complement's higher price lowers it. Tastes, expected future prices and buyer numbers can also shift demand.
items.zh: 收入增加令正常品需求增、劣等品需求減；替代品價格升令本品需求增，互補品價格升令本品需求減。喜好、預期及買家數也影響需求。
items.example: Example 例：Gasoline and cars are complements. More expensive gasoline can reduce demand for cars, shifting car demand left. 汽油更貴會降低汽車需求。
items.question: Tea substitutes for coffee. Tea price rises. Coffee demand? 茶價升時咖啡需求？
options: Increases / 增加
Decreases / 減少
Only moves along coffee demand / 只沿線
Must stay fixed / 必不變
items.why: Some buyers switch from tea to coffee at each coffee price.

items.objective: Predict supply shifts caused by input prices, production technology, expectations and the number of sellers.
items.title: Supply determinants / 供給因素
items.en: Lower input costs, improved production technology or more sellers usually increase supply. Higher input costs reduce it. Expectations can alter current supply when production or storage can be shifted over time.
items.zh: 投入成本下降、技術改善或賣家增加通常令供給增加；成本升令供給減少。若能調整生產或存貨，未來價格預期也影響當期供給。
items.example: Example 例：Cheaper steel reduces the cost of making trucks; truck supply shifts right, lowering equilibrium price and raising quantity if demand is unchanged. 鋼價下降令卡車供給增加。
items.question: A new machine lowers unit production cost. Which shift is expected? 新機器降低成本？
options: Only movement along supply / 只沿供給線移動
Supply right / 供給右移
Supply left / 供給左移
Demand left / 需求左移
items.why: At each price, production becomes more attractive.

items.objective: Add individual quantities horizontally at each price to obtain market demand or market supply.
items.title: Market aggregation / 市場曲線加總
items.en: Add individual quantities at the same price. This is horizontal summation because quantity is on the horizontal axis. Do not add prices or include negative supplies or demands when an individual would choose zero.
items.zh: 在同一價格把各人的數量相加；因數量在橫軸，稱橫向加總。不可把價格相加；當個人選擇零時，不加入負數。
items.example: Example 例：At P=$4, A demands 3 units and B demands 5. Market demand is 3+5=8 units. 同價下加總數量。
items.question: At P=$10, three firms supply 2, 0 and 7 units. Market supply? 市場供給量？
items.why: 2+0+7=9 at that price.

items.objective: Find equilibrium in a graph, schedule or equations by setting `Qd = Qs` and solving for price and quantity.
items.title: Solving equilibrium / 求均衡
items.en: Equilibrium equates quantity demanded and supplied at one price. Solve the equations together, then substitute the price back into either equation and check both give the same quantity.
items.zh: 均衡要求同一價格下 Qd=Qs。聯立求 P，再代回兩式檢查數量一致。
items.example: Example 例：Qs=2P and Qd=300−P. 2P=300−P gives P=100 and Q=200. 兩式皆得到 200。
items.question: Qs=P, Qd=60−2P. Equilibrium P and Q? 均衡？
items.why: 3P=60, so P=20 and Q=20.

items.objective: Identify a shortage (`Qd > Qs`) or surplus (`Qs > Qd`) at a stated price and explain the usual pressure on price in an unrestricted market.
items.title: Shortage and surplus / 短缺與過剩
items.en: Below equilibrium, Qd exceeds Qs and buyers compete for scarce supply, creating upward price pressure. Above equilibrium, Qs exceeds Qd and unsold stock creates downward pressure. A shortage or surplus is a difference between desired quantities.
items.zh: 低於均衡價時 Qd>Qs，有升價壓力；高於均衡價時 Qs>Qd，有降價壓力。短缺或過剩是意欲買賣數量的差額。
items.example: Example 例：At P=8, Qd=30 and Qs=18. Shortage=12; unrestricted price tends upward. 短缺十二單位。
items.question: At a given price Qs=50, Qd=35. What pressure occurs? 供五十、需三十五？
options: Surplus 15, price down / 過剩十五、價降
Shortage 15, price up / 短缺十五、價升
Surplus 85, price up / 過剩八十五、價升
Equilibrium / 均衡
items.why: Qs−Qd=15 units are unsold at that price.

items.objective: Work out the direction of equilibrium price and quantity after one curve shifts. For simultaneous shifts, identify which outcome is definite and which depends on the relative shift sizes.
items.title: One or two shifts / 單一及雙重移動
items.en: D rising raises both equilibrium P and Q; S rising lowers P and raises Q. Reverse shifts reverse those signs. If both curves move, combine the effects: an outcome is definite only when both shifts push it in the same direction.
items.zh: D 增加令 P、Q 升；S 增加令 P 降、Q 升，反向移動結果相反。雙線移動時，只有兩個效果同向的變數能直接確定。
items.example: Example 例：D and S both rise. Each raises Q, so Q rises; their effects on P oppose, so P is ambiguous. 需求供給同增，量升而價未定。
items.question: D rises while S falls. What is definite? 需求增、供給減，何者確定？
options: P falls; Q rises / 價跌量升
P rises; Q ambiguous / 價升、量未定
Q rises; P ambiguous / 量升、價未定
P and Q both fall / 均下降
items.why: Both changes push price up; quantity effects oppose.

items.objective: Follow a chain across markets: for example, an input-price change affects a final good, which affects demand for a complement or substitute.
items.title: Linked markets / 跨市場傳導
items.en: Identify the first market's shock and equilibrium response, then use related-good or input relationships to shift another market's curve. Keep movements along a curve separate from shifts in the next market.
items.zh: 先分析第一個市場的衝擊，再利用投入品、替代品或互補品關係傳到下一市場。每一步都重新辨認移動哪條線。
items.example: Example 例：Cheaper TV production raises TV supply, lowers TV price and increases demand for complementary streaming services. 電視便宜令串流服務需求增加。
items.question: Fuel costs rise for airlines; air travel and hotels are complements. Hotel demand likely? 航空燃料更貴，機票與酒店互補，酒店需求？
options: Hotel supply must rise / 酒店供給必升
Hotel demand becomes vertical / 需求變垂直
Falls / 下降
Rises / 上升
items.why: Costlier flights reduce travel and associated hotel demand, holding other factors fixed.

items.objective: Work backward from observed changes in price and quantity to determine which proposed demand or supply shift could explain them; identify when more than one explanation is possible.
items.title: Diagnosing observed changes / 從結果推斷衝擊
items.en: A higher P with higher Q is consistent with a demand increase alone; higher P with lower Q fits a supply decrease alone. These patterns identify possible single-shift explanations, but simultaneous shifts may also generate them.
items.zh: 價量同升可由需求增加解釋；價升量跌可由供給減少解釋。但多個因素同時改變也可有相同結果，不能把單線解釋當成唯一原因。
items.example: Example 例：Truck price rises while sales fall. More expensive steel shifting supply left fits this pattern. 鋼材成本上升可解釋價升量跌。
items.question: Price falls and quantity rises. Which single shift fits? 價跌量升符合哪個單一移動？
options: Supply decreases / 供給減少
Demand increases / 需求增加
Demand decreases / 需求減少
Supply increases / 供給增加
items.why: An outward supply shift moves equilibrium down the demand curve.

items.objective: Calculate price elasticity of demand as the absolute percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. When comparing two points, use the midpoint formula: `|[(Q2−Q1)/((Q1+Q2)/2)] / [(P2−P1)/((P1+P2)/2)]|`.
items.title: Midpoint elasticity / 中點法彈性
items.en: Price elasticity of demand is the absolute percentage quantity change divided by percentage price change. Use the average of the two endpoints as each denominator so reversing the direction gives the same result.
items.zh: 需求價格彈性用數量百分比變化除價格百分比變化，再取絕對值。中點法以兩點平均數為分母，避免方向影響結果。
items.question: P:4→6, Q:12→8. Midpoint Ed? 中點法彈性？

items.objective: Classify demand as elastic (`> 1`), inelastic (`< 1`), unit elastic (`= 1`), perfectly inelastic (`= 0`) or perfectly elastic. Identify horizontal and vertical extreme cases.
items.title: Classifying elasticity / 彈性分類
items.en: Ed>1 is elastic, Ed<1 inelastic, and Ed=1 unit elastic. Vertical demand is perfectly inelastic with Ed=0. Horizontal demand is perfectly elastic in the idealized limit. Classify using percentage responses, not visual angle alone.
items.zh: Ed 大於一有彈性，小於一缺乏彈性，等於一為單位彈性。垂直需求完全無彈性；水平需求完全有彈性。圖線斜度還受單位及軸比例影響。
items.example: Example 例：A 10% price rise reduces Q by 3%, so Ed=0.3 and demand is inelastic. 價升一成、量跌百分之三。
items.question: A perfectly vertical demand curve has which elasticity? 垂直需求彈性？
options: Infinity / 無限大
items.why: Quantity does not respond to price. 數量不隨價格變。

items.objective: Explain how availability of substitutes, necessity versus luxury, market definition and time horizon influence elasticity.
items.title: Determinants of elasticity / 彈性決定因素
items.en: Close substitutes make switching easier; narrowly defined goods tend to have more substitutes. Necessities tend to be less elastic than luxuries, and longer adjustment time generally increases responsiveness.
items.zh: 替代品多便容易轉換；商品定義較窄通常有更多替代品。必需品通常較缺乏彈性，時間較長通常更能調整。
items.example: Example 例：Demand for one brand of bottled water is likely more elastic than demand for drinking water overall. 單一品牌比整體食水更易被替代。
items.question: Which demand is usually more elastic, other things equal? 一般何者更有彈性？
options: Essential emergency care / 必需急救
A good with no substitutes / 無替代品商品
One coffee brand / 單一咖啡品牌
All beverages / 所有飲料
items.why: A narrowly defined brand has many close alternatives.

items.objective: Distinguish elasticity from slope. On a linear demand curve, elasticity changes along the curve; a constant slope does not imply constant elasticity.
items.title: Elasticity versus slope / 彈性與斜率
items.en: Slope uses absolute changes in P and Q; elasticity uses percentage changes. On linear demand Q=a−bP, Ed=bP/Q. It is higher near the high-price, low-quantity end even though slope is constant.
items.zh: 斜率用單位變化，彈性用百分比。線性需求 Q=a−bP 的 Ed=bP/Q；高價低量端彈性大，斜率仍相同。
items.example: Example 例：For Q=100−P, Ed at P=80,Q=20 is 4; at P=20,Q=80 it is 0.25. 同線不同點的彈性不同。
items.question: For Q=100−P at P=50,Q=50, Ed is? 彈性多少？

items.objective: Relate price changes to total revenue or expenditure `P × Q`: a price increase raises revenue when demand is inelastic and lowers it when demand is elastic; the reverse applies to a price decrease, holding the demand curve fixed.
items.title: Revenue test / 總收入判斷
items.en: Along a fixed demand curve, a price rise raises total revenue when demand is inelastic and lowers it when demand is elastic. Reverse the direction for a price cut. For large changes crossing elasticity regions, calculate P×Q directly.
items.zh: 沿固定需求線，缺乏彈性時價升令收入增；有彈性時價升令收入減。減價時反向；大幅變動跨越不同彈性區域時直接算 P×Q。
items.example: Example 例：P rises from 5 to 6, Q falls from 5 to 4.5. Revenue rises from 25 to 27; the quantity response is relatively small. 價升幅度勝過量跌。
items.question: Along an elastic demand segment, a small price cut causes TR to do what? 有彈性需求區減價？
options: Rise / 上升
Fall / 下降
Always stay fixed / 必不變
Become negative / 變負
items.why: The percentage quantity gain exceeds the percentage price reduction.

items.objective: Interpret zero and unit elasticity in verbal situations, including fixed quantity purchased and fixed expenditure.
items.title: Fixed quantity or spending / 固定數量或支出
items.en: A buyer who always buys the same quantity has zero price elasticity. A buyer who always spends the same amount has Q=k/P, giving unit elasticity. These are statements about behavior across prices.
items.zh: 每次購買固定數量代表零彈性；每次固定支出時 Q=k/P，代表單位彈性。須看價格改變時的購買規則。
items.example: Example 例：“Five liters regardless of price” means Ed=0. “$20 of fuel regardless of price” means Ed=1. 固定公升與固定金額不同。
items.question: A buyer always buys $30 of rice. Price elasticity? 每次買三十元米？
options: Infinity / 無限大
items.why: Fixed expenditure means P×Q is constant, so demand is unit elastic.

items.objective: Calculate and interpret income elasticity and cross-price elasticity; use their signs to classify normal/inferior goods and substitutes/complements.
items.title: Income & cross-price elasticity / 收入與交叉彈性
items.en: Income elasticity is %ΔQd/%Δincome: positive for normal goods, negative for inferior goods. Cross-price elasticity is %ΔQd of A/%ΔP of B: positive for substitutes, negative for complements.
items.zh: 收入彈性正值屬正常品，負值屬劣等品。交叉價格彈性正值屬替代品，負值屬互補品；計算時保留正負號。
items.example: Example 例：Tea price rises 10%, coffee demand rises 5%. Cross elasticity=+0.5, suggesting substitutes. 咖啡需求隨茶價同向。
items.question: Income rises 10%, demand falls 5%. Income elasticity and classification? 收入增、需求減？
options: −2, substitute / 替代品
+2, complement / 互補品
−0.5, inferior / 劣等品
+0.5, normal / 正常品
items.why: −5%/10%=−0.5; demand falls with income.

items.objective: Calculate price elasticity of supply using percentage changes and explain why supply is often more elastic over a longer horizon.
items.title: Supply elasticity / 供給彈性
items.en: Supply elasticity is the percentage quantity supplied response divided by the percentage price change. A longer horizon often permits new capacity, entry or changed inputs, making supply more elastic; this is a tendency, not a universal law.
items.zh: 供給彈性用供給量百分比反應除價格百分比變化。長期可改變設備、投入或企業數目，通常更有彈性。
items.example: Example 例：P rises 10%, Qs rises 20%; Es=2. Firms may respond more over a year than over a day. 供給反應大於價格變化。
items.question: A 5% price rise increases supply by 15%. Es? 供給彈性？

items.objective: Apply elasticity to shifts: explain how the size of a price or quantity response depends on the elasticity of the curve being moved along.
items.title: Elasticity and shock size / 彈性與衝擊反應
items.en: After a curve shifts, the elasticity of the other curve shapes the price and quantity adjustment. A less responsive demand curve generally produces a larger price change and smaller quantity change for a comparable supply shock.
items.zh: 一條曲線移動時，另一條線的彈性影響新均衡。相同供給衝擊下，需求較缺乏彈性通常令價格變較多、數量變較少。
items.example: Example 例：A supply cut in essential fuel can cause a sharp price rise in the short run when demand barely responds. 短期必需燃料難以減用。
items.question: Same supply reduction, which demand gives the larger price rise? 同樣供給減少，哪種需求令價升較多？
options: More inelastic / 較缺乏彈性
More elastic / 較有彈性
Perfectly horizontal / 完全水平
Elasticity cannot matter / 彈性無影響
items.why: Less quantity adjustment requires more price adjustment.

items.objective: Analyze the revenue effects of a bumper crop versus a local crop failure, and supply restrictions in oil or illegal drugs; trace effects into related markets when needed.
items.title: Crop and restriction applications / 農作物與限制供給
items.en: A broad supply increase can lower revenue when market demand is inelastic. A local producer faces more substitutes for its output, so a local crop loss can reduce its revenue. Restricting oil or drug supply can raise spending when demand is inelastic; linked complements may also be affected.
items.zh: 整體豐收可能因需求缺乏彈性而令總收入減少；局部農民面對其他地區替代品，失收可能降低自身收入。限制油或毒品供給可令價格及支出上升。
items.example: Example 例：Worldwide grain supply expands; price falls sharply and purchases rise slightly, reducing total farm revenue. 全球穀物豐收可能令農民總收入下降。
items.question: Supply of an inelastically demanded drug falls. User spending may do what? 毒品供給減、需求缺乏彈性，支出可能？
options: Equal zero / 等於零
Rise / 上升
Always fall / 必下降
Stay fixed by definition / 定義上固定
items.why: The price increase can outweigh the quantity reduction along demand.

items.objective: Evaluate proposed explanations for a price change with unchanged quantity, including perfectly inelastic curves and simultaneous shifts.
items.title: Price changes with fixed quantity / 價變但量不變
items.en: A demand increase with vertical supply can raise price without changing quantity. A supply decrease with vertical demand can do the same. Opposing quantity effects from simultaneous shifts are another possibility.
items.zh: 需求增配合垂直供給可令價升量不變；供給減配合垂直需求也可。雙線移動的數量效果互相抵消也是可能原因。
items.example: Example 例：A venue has a fixed 1,000 seats. Increased demand can raise ticket price while seats sold remain 1,000. 座位供應固定。
items.question: P rises while Q is unchanged. Which explanation is possible? 價升量不變何解釋可能？
options: Demand falls with upward supply / 需求跌、供給向上
Supply rises with downward demand / 供給增、需求向下
Demand rises with vertical supply / 需求增、供給垂直
Supply rises with horizontal demand / 供給增、需求水平
items.why: Vertical supply fixes quantity despite a demand shift.

title: Chapter 6 — Supply, Demand, and Government Policies

items.objective: Identify a binding price ceiling below equilibrium and a binding price floor above equilibrium; recognize when a control has no effect and why.
items.title: Binding controls / 有約束力的管制
items.en: A ceiling is a legal maximum and binds below the free-market equilibrium price. A floor is a legal minimum and binds above equilibrium. A control on the other side of equilibrium leaves the equilibrium available.
items.zh: 價格上限在均衡價以下才具約束力；價格下限在均衡價以上才具約束力。若原均衡仍合法，市場可留在原均衡。
items.example: Example 例：P*=100. A ceiling of 90 binds; a floor of 90 does not. 同樣九十元，上限與下限效果不同。
items.question: Equilibrium price is $20. Which control binds? 均衡價二十元，何者具約束力？
options: Floor $20 with no excess / 下限二十且無過剩
Ceiling $25 / 上限二十五
Floor $15 / 下限十五
Ceiling $15 / 上限十五
items.why: A $15 maximum prevents the market reaching its $20 equilibrium.

items.objective: Calculate quantity demanded, quantity supplied, actual traded quantity, and the resulting shortage or surplus at a controlled price. With ordinary voluntary trading and no government purchase, the short side limits the amount traded.
items.title: Traded quantity under controls / 管制下交易量
items.en: Calculate Qd and Qs separately at the controlled price. A shortage is Qd−Qs; a surplus is Qs−Qd. With voluntary trade and no government buying or extra supply, actual trade is limited by the smaller quantity.
items.zh: 把管制價分別代入供需，短缺為 Qd−Qs，過剩為 Qs−Qd。自願交易且政府不額外買賣時，實際交易量取較小數。
items.example: Example 例：At a floor, Qd=40 and Qs=70. Surplus=30, but only 40 units are sold. 想出售七十不代表售出七十。
items.question: At a ceiling Qd=90 and Qs=60. Quantity sold and shortage? 上限下需九十、供六十？
options: Sold 60, shortage 30 / 售六十、缺三十
Sold 90, shortage 30 / 售九十、缺三十
Sold 30, shortage 60 / 售三十、缺六十
Sold 150, shortage 0 / 售一百五十、無缺
items.why: The supply side limits trade to 60 units.

items.objective: Explain non-price rationing, queues and potential quality changes under a binding ceiling; explain unsold supply under a binding floor.
items.title: Rationing and quality / 配給與品質
items.en: A binding ceiling creates excess demand, so price no longer alone selects buyers: queues, waiting lists or favoritism may emerge. Sellers can also reduce quality. A binding floor leaves some willing sellers unable to sell.
items.zh: 上限造成需求過多，可能靠排隊、名單或偏好分配；賣家也可能減少維修或品質。下限造成過剩，部分賣家無法出售。
items.example: Example 例：Under rent control, apartments have waiting lists and landlords may reduce maintenance when rent cannot reflect quality. 租金限制可改變維修誘因。
items.question: A binding rent ceiling may produce which result? 有約束力的租金上限可能？
options: Automatic efficient rationing / 自動有效率配給
Waiting lists and lower maintenance / 等候名單、維修減少
Guaranteed housing for every applicant / 人人必有屋
Excess vacant supply from the ceiling alone / 單靠上限造成過剩
items.why: The shortage requires non-price allocation; quality incentives can weaken.

items.objective: Apply a minimum wage to the labor market: workers supply labor, firms demand labor, employment is labor demanded at a binding wage floor, and unemployment is labor supplied minus labor demanded.
items.title: Minimum wage and employment / 最低工資與就業
items.en: Workers supply labor and firms demand it. At a binding minimum wage, employment equals labor demanded and unemployment in this simple diagram equals labor supplied minus labor demanded.
items.zh: 工人供應勞工，企業需求勞工。最低工資高於均衡時，就業取企業需求量，圖中的失業為勞工供給減需求。
items.example: Example 例：At the wage floor, 120 workers want jobs and firms hire 80. Employment=80 and unemployment=40. 想工作的人不等於成功就業者。
items.question: At the minimum wage Ls=100 and Ld=70. Employment? 就業人數？
items.why: Firms hire 70; the remaining 30 willing workers lack jobs in this model.

items.objective: Calculate total wage payments as wage times employment. Use the elasticity of labor demand to assess how a wage increase affects total payments; use both labor supply and demand responses to assess unemployment.
items.title: Wage bill and elasticities / 工資總額與彈性
items.en: Total wage payments equal wage times employment. Along inelastic labor demand, a wage rise reduces employment proportionately less, raising the wage bill. Unemployment changes depend on both labor demand and labor supply responses.
items.zh: 總工資為工資乘就業。勞工需求缺乏彈性時，工資升幅超過就業跌幅，總支付上升；失業變化則同時涉及供給與需求。
items.example: Example 例：Wage 10→12 and employment 100→95: total payments 1,000→1,140. 勞工總收入上升，但五人失去工作。
items.question: A small wage increase on elastic labor demand does what to total wage payments? 有彈性勞工需求下小幅加薪？
options: Always leaves them unchanged / 必不變
Equals unemployment / 等於失業
Raises them / 增加
Lowers them / 減少
items.why: The employment percentage decline exceeds the wage percentage rise.

items.objective: Compare short- and long-run shortages when supply and demand become more elastic, as in rent control.
items.title: Short-run versus long-run shortage / 短長期短缺
items.en: At a fixed rent ceiling, more elastic long-run supply can reduce housing offered more, while more elastic demand raises desired quantity more. Together these can enlarge the shortage relative to the short run.
items.zh: 租金上限固定時，長期供給更能收縮，需求更能增加，短缺因而可能比短期更大。比較時要固定其他條件及原均衡。
items.example: Example 例：Short run Qd=110, Qs=90 gives shortage 20; long run Qd=130, Qs=70 gives shortage 60. 長期調整令短缺擴大。
items.question: With the same binding ceiling and more responsive supply and demand, shortage generally? 同上限、供需更有彈性？
options: Grows / 增大
Must vanish / 必消失
Becomes negative always / 必變負
Equals tax revenue / 等於稅收
items.why: Both responses can widen Qd−Qs.

items.objective: Assess consumer and producer surplus under controls carefully: the identity of buyers or sellers who actually trade matters. Without an efficient-rationing assumption, the exact welfare areas may not be determined from supply and demand curves alone.
items.title: Rationing and surplus / 配給與剩餘
items.en: Surplus depends on who receives or supplies the traded units. The usual maximum-surplus areas under a control assume high-value buyers receive goods and low-cost sellers supply them. Random or discriminatory allocation can reduce surplus further.
items.zh: 管制後的剩餘取決於誰成功買賣。常見圖形面積假設商品到最高價值買家、由最低成本賣家供應；隨機或偏好配給可再減少剩餘。
items.example: Example 例：One unit costs $2. At a $3 ceiling, allocating it to a buyer valuing it at $10 gives total surplus $8; to a $5 buyer gives $3. 同交易量，配給不同令剩餘不同。
items.question: Under a shortage, can exact CS always be calculated without knowing who buys? 不知誰買到時可必定算出 CS？
options: Yes, price alone fixes CS / 價格已足夠
No, allocation matters / 配給重要
Yes, Qd is quantity sold / Qd 就是售量
No, because CS is always zero / CS 必零
items.why: Buyer valuations among actual recipients determine CS.

items.objective: Draw or interpret a tax on sellers as an upward supply shift, and a tax on buyers as a downward demand shift, by the tax per unit.
items.title: Drawing a unit tax / 畫單位稅
items.en: A tax on sellers shifts supply vertically up by t in buyer-price terms. A tax on buyers shifts demand vertically down by t in seller-price terms. Both create the same gap Pb−Ps=t under the standard model.
items.zh: 向賣方收稅，可在買方價格座標把供給上移 t；向買方收稅，可在賣方價格座標把需求下移 t。結果均是 Pb 比 Ps 高 t。
items.example: Example 例：If sellers need net $10 to supply a quantity, a $3 tax means buyers must pay $13 for that quantity. 淨收十元需要買方付十三元。
items.question: A $4 unit tax on sellers shifts supply by how much vertically? 賣方每件四元稅？
options: Right 4 units / 右移四件
No wedge / 沒有稅楔
Up $4 / 上移四元
Down $4 / 下移四元
items.why: At each quantity, the buyer price must cover the old supply price plus tax.

items.objective: Solve for the buyer's price `Pb`, seller's net price `Ps`, and quantity using `Pb − Ps = tax`, `Qd(Pb) = Qs(Ps)`.
items.title: Tax equilibrium / 稅後均衡
items.en: Use separate price variables: demand depends on Pb and supply on Ps. Solve Qd(Pb)=Qs(Ps) together with Pb−Ps=t. Substituting a single price into both original curves without the wedge loses the tax.
items.zh: 需求用買方價 Pb，供給用賣方淨價 Ps，再聯立 Pb−Ps=t。不可在原供需兩式都用同一價格而漏掉稅楔。
items.example: Example 例：Qs=2Ps, Qd=300−Pb, t=30. Pb=Ps+30 gives 2Ps=270−Ps; Ps=90, Pb=120, Q=180.
items.question: Qs=Ps, Qd=100−Pb and t=20. Seller price? 賣方淨價？

items.objective: Calculate the buyer's per-unit burden `Pb − P0` and seller's per-unit burden `P0 − Ps`, where `P0` is the original price; the burdens sum to the tax.
items.title: Per-unit tax burden / 每單位稅負
items.en: Compare each post-tax price with the original equilibrium P0. Buyers bear Pb−P0, sellers bear P0−Ps, and these add to t. Total burdens across traded units multiply these amounts by the post-tax quantity.
items.zh: 買方每件負擔 Pb−P0，賣方每件負擔 P0−Ps，合計為 t。要算交易單位上的總負擔，再乘稅後數量。
items.example: Example 例：P0=100, Pb=120, Ps=90. Buyers bear 20 and sellers 10; total unit tax=30. 買方負擔三分之二。
items.question: P0=50, Pb=56, Ps=46. Seller's burden per unit? 賣方每件負擔？
items.why: 50−46=4. The remaining 6 is borne by buyers.

items.objective: Explain why economic incidence depends on relative elasticities rather than the side legally required to remit the tax: the less elastic side generally bears more.
items.title: Elasticity and incidence / 彈性與稅負
items.en: The relatively less elastic side has fewer effective alternatives, so it typically absorbs more of a unit tax. Legal responsibility for remitting the tax does not determine the economic burden.
items.zh: 相對缺乏彈性的一方較難調整，通常承擔較多稅負。法定把錢交政府的一方與最終承擔負擔的一方須分清。
items.example: Example 例：If supply is very elastic while demand is steep, buyers bear most of a small tax. 供給容易退出，買家較難避開稅負。
items.question: Demand is perfectly inelastic and supply slopes up. Who bears the unit tax? 需求垂直、供給向上，誰承擔？
options: Whoever remits it / 依法定繳稅方
Buyers / 買家
Sellers / 賣家
Always half each / 必各半
items.why: Quantity stays fixed and the buyer price absorbs the wedge in this model.

items.objective: Apply the same reasoning to payroll taxes and identify employer labor cost versus the wage received by workers.
items.title: Payroll taxes / 工資稅
items.en: Treat labor as the traded service. Firms are buyers paying total labor cost; workers are sellers receiving net wages. The gap equals the payroll tax. Changing which side legally pays an unchanged total tax does not by itself alter incidence.
items.zh: 把勞工當交易服務，企業支付總勞工成本，工人收到淨工資；差額是工資稅。總稅不變時，改由哪一方繳稅本身不改變經濟歸宿。
items.example: Example 例：Employer cost $110, worker net wage $95: payroll tax wedge=$15. 企業成本和工人淨收不能混用。
items.question: Employer pays $120 per hour and worker receives $100. Tax wedge? 工資稅楔多少？
