title: Chapter 7 — Consumers, Producers, and the Efficiency of Markets

items.objective: Interpret willingness to pay, the demand curve and the marginal buyer. Compute consumer surplus as willingness to pay minus the price paid, summed over units purchased.
items.title: Willingness to pay and CS / 願付價格與消費者剩餘
items.en: Willingness to pay is a buyer's maximum valuation for a unit. Buy units valued at least as highly as the price. Consumer surplus sums WTP−price over units purchased; the demand curve shows the marginal unit's valuation.
items.zh: 願付價格是每單位最高估值。只買價值至少等於價格的單位；CS 把已購單位的價值減付款加總，需求線顯示邊際買家估值。
items.example: Example 例：WTP for three units is 7,5,3 and P=4. Buy two; CS=(7−4)+(5−4)=4.
items.question: WTP is 9,6,2 and P=5. CS? 願付九、六、二，價格五？
items.why: Buy the first two units; (9−5)+(6−5)=5.

items.objective: Interpret sellers' opportunity costs, the supply curve and the marginal seller. Compute producer surplus as the price received minus cost, summed over units sold.
items.title: Costs and PS / 成本與生產者剩餘
items.en: A seller's cost measures the opportunity cost of supplying a unit. Producer surplus sums price−cost over units sold; supply gives the marginal seller's cost. With fixed costs, PS generally differs from profit by fixed cost.
items.zh: 賣方成本是供應單位的機會成本。PS 是售出單位的價格減成本總和；供給線顯示邊際成本。存在固定成本時，PS 通常等於利潤加固定成本。
items.example: Example 例：Unit costs 1,3,5 and P=4. Sell two; PS=(4−1)+(4−3)=4.
items.question: Unit costs 2,4,7 and P=6. PS? 成本二、四、七，價格六？
items.why: Sell the first two: (6−2)+(6−4)=6.

items.objective: Identify consumer surplus as the area below demand and above the buyer's price, and producer surplus as the area above supply and below the seller's price, over the units actually traded.
items.title: Surplus areas / 剩餘面積
items.en: CS lies below demand and above buyer price; PS lies above supply and below seller price. Integrate only over units actually traded. When tax creates two prices, use Pb for CS and Ps for PS.
items.zh: CS 在需求線下、買方價格上；PS 在供給線上、賣方價格下，只計至實際交易量。有稅時兩邊使用不同價格。
items.example: Example 例：Linear demand intercept 10, P=6, Q=4 gives CS=½×4×(10−6)=8. 以實際交易四單位作三角形底。
items.question: Demand intercept 12, P=8, traded Q=4. CS? 線性需求下 CS？
items.why: Triangle area=½×4×4=8.

items.objective: Use rectangles, triangles or discrete unit values to calculate and compare surplus as prices change. Separate gains to existing participants from gains to new participants.
items.title: Changes in surplus / 剩餘變化
items.en: A lower price benefits existing buyers on all units they already buy and may attract additional purchases. Separate the existing-unit rectangle from the new-unit triangle. For discrete values, sum unit gains directly.
items.zh: 減價讓原有購買量每件都得益，也吸引額外購買。可分原有單位長方形與新增單位三角形；離散題逐件加總。
items.example: Example 例：Linear demand: price falls 6→4 and Q rises 4→6. Existing gain=(6−4)×4=8; new-unit gain=½×2×2=2; total CS gain=10.
items.question: Price falls $2; existing purchases are 5 units. Gain on existing units alone? 舊購買量五件，減價兩元，舊單位收益？
items.why: Each of five existing units saves $2, so the rectangle is $10.

items.objective: Compare a fixed-fee service with a per-use charge: identify the marginal cost faced by the consumer, the quantity chosen and net benefit after the fixed fee.
items.title: Fixed fee versus per use / 固定費與按次收費
items.en: Choose usage using the marginal price, then subtract all payments including fixed fees from total willingness to pay. A fixed fee affects whether to subscribe, while a zero per-use price can increase usage after subscribing.
items.zh: 使用量取決於邊際價格；比較整體淨收益時要扣所有付款，包括固定費。固定費影響是否訂閱，訂閱後的零邊際費可增加使用。
items.example: Example 例：Demand Q=10−P. Free usage plus $20 fee yields Q=10, total value=50 and net surplus=30. Per-use price $2 yields Q=8 and CS=32. 按次方案淨收益較高。
items.question: For Q=10−P with per-use P=2 and no fixed fee, quantity? 每次兩元，觀看量？
items.why: Q=10−2=8; a fixed fee would enter the net-benefit comparison separately.

items.objective: Calculate total surplus as consumer surplus plus producer surplus, or buyers' total value minus sellers' total cost in an untaxed market.
items.title: Total surplus / 總剩餘
items.en: In an untaxed market, payments transfer value between buyer and seller. Adding CS and PS cancels the payment, leaving total value to buyers minus total opportunity cost to sellers.
items.zh: 無稅市場內，買方付款等於賣方收入，兩者相加抵消；總剩餘是買方總價值減賣方總機會成本。
items.example: Example 例：WTP=20, price=12, cost=7. CS=8, PS=5, total=13=20−7. 價格影響分配但這筆交易總收益為十三。
items.question: WTP=30, price=18, cost=10. Total surplus? 總剩餘？
items.why: CS=12 plus PS=8 gives 20; also 30−10=20.

items.objective: Explain why, in the competitive model without relevant market failures, the equilibrium quantity maximizes total surplus: trade units for which marginal value is at least marginal cost.
items.title: Efficient equilibrium / 有效率均衡
items.en: In a competitive market without relevant market failures, trade units for which marginal buyer value exceeds marginal cost. At equilibrium, marginal value equals marginal cost; increasing or decreasing quantity from that point cannot raise total surplus.
items.zh: 沒有相關市場失靈的競爭模型中，應完成邊際價值高於成本的交易。均衡使兩者相等，偏離該數量會失去總剩餘。
items.example: Example 例：An extra unit valued at $9 costs $6. Making it adds $3 surplus, so output below that unit leaves gains unrealized. 這項交易增加三元總收益。
items.question: Marginal value is $8 and marginal cost $5. Efficient action? 邊際價值八、成本五？
options: Only produce if price is zero / 價零才生產
Produce this unit / 生產該單位
Do not produce it / 不生產
Ignore both values / 不考慮兩者
items.why: The unit adds $3 to total surplus.

items.objective: Identify lost gains from trade when quantity is below the efficient level, and the loss from units whose marginal cost exceeds marginal value when quantity is above it.
items.title: Underproduction and overproduction / 過少與過多生產
items.en: Below efficient quantity, some omitted units have value above cost, creating unrealized gains. Above it, extra units cost more than their value. Both reduce total surplus relative to efficient output.
items.zh: 產量不足會漏掉價值高於成本的交易；產量過多會完成成本高於價值的交易。兩者均減少相對有效率水平的總剩餘。
items.example: Example 例：An unnecessary unit worth $4 costs $7, reducing surplus by $3. 過量的一件令總剩餘少三元。
items.question: An extra unit has value $2 and cost $6. Its effect on total surplus? 額外單位的效果？
items.why: 2−6=−4, so the unit is inefficient.

items.objective: Distinguish efficiency from equality and identify circumstances, including market power and externalities, where the simple competitive-efficiency conclusion may not hold.
items.title: Efficiency assumptions / 效率假設
items.en: Efficiency maximizes total surplus; equality concerns distribution. The competitive-efficiency result assumes conditions such as price taking and no relevant external effects. Market power or externalities can break the result.
items.zh: 效率最大化總剩餘，平等關心分配。市場效率結論依賴價格接受及無相關外部性等條件；壟斷力量或外部影響可破壞結論。
items.example: Example 例：A market may maximize buyer-plus-seller surplus yet impose pollution costs on residents. Social surplus must include these costs. 必須加入第三方成本。
items.question: Which issue can invalidate the simple competitive-efficiency conclusion? 何者可能推翻簡單效率結論？
options: A buyer using cash / 買家用現金
A labeled quantity axis / 數量軸有標籤
Different shirt colors alone / 只有衫色不同
Unpriced pollution / 未計價污染
items.why: An external cost is omitted from private supply and demand.

items.objective: Apply marginal analysis to insurance: compare the consumer's out-of-pocket price with society's marginal cost, and explain the possible effect on the quantity of care.
items.title: Insurance and excessive use / 保險與過量使用
items.en: When a patient's out-of-pocket price is below the true marginal social cost, the patient may choose units valued above their own payment but below society's cost. Fixed premiums do not add to the marginal price of a procedure.
items.zh: 病人自付低於社會邊際成本時，可能使用價值高於自付但低於成本的服務。保費若不隨使用次數改變，不增加每項服務的邊際價格。
items.example: Example 例：A procedure worth $60 costs society $100; the insured patient pays $20. It is privately attractive but reduces total surplus by $40. 私人想做，社會淨損四十。
items.question: Value=$70, social cost=$100, copayment=$20. Social surplus from the procedure? 總剩餘變化？
items.why: 70−100=−30; the copayment is not the total resource cost.

title: Chapter 8 — Application: The Costs of Taxation

items.objective: On a supply-and-demand graph, identify the pretax equilibrium, the tax wedge, the prices paid and received, and the quantity traded after the tax.
items.title: Reading a tax diagram / 讀稅收圖
items.en: Locate the original intersection at P0,Q0. After tax, read buyer price from demand and seller price from supply at the same lower quantity Qt. Their vertical difference is the unit tax.
items.zh: 先找稅前交點 P0、Q0。稅後在同一個較低交易量 Qt，從需求讀 Pb、供給讀 Ps；垂直差額就是單位稅。
items.example: Example 例：P0=100,Q0=200; after tax Pb=120,Ps=90,Qt=180. The wedge is 30 and quantity falls 20.
items.question: Tax diagram gives Pb=14,Ps=10 at Qt=50. Unit tax? 單位稅？
items.why: The tax wedge is 14−10=4 per unit, not total revenue.

items.objective: Calculate government revenue as `tax per unit × quantity traded after tax`; distinguish buyer spending `Pb × Q` from seller receipts `Ps × Q`.
items.title: Revenue versus spending / 稅收、支出與收入
items.en: Government revenue is t times post-tax quantity. Buyers spend Pb×Qt, while sellers receive net receipts Ps×Qt. The difference between these two amounts is government tax revenue.
items.zh: 政府稅收是 t 乘稅後交易量；買方支出為 Pb×Qt，賣方淨收為 Ps×Qt，差額就是稅收。
items.example: Example 例：Pb=12,Ps=9,Q=100. Buyer spending=1,200; seller receipts=900; government revenue=300. 三個金額需分開。
items.question: t=5 and post-tax Q=80. Government revenue? 政府收入？
items.why: 5×80=400. Use post-tax quantity.

items.objective: Compute consumer surplus, producer surplus and government revenue after a tax. In the standard model, total surplus is `CS + PS + tax revenue`.
items.title: Post-tax welfare / 稅後福利
items.en: CS is computed using Pb, PS using Ps, and government revenue must be added to both. This counts tax payments as transfers within the standard welfare calculation rather than treating all tax as lost value.
items.zh: CS 用 Pb，PS 用 Ps，再加政府收入。稅款在標準福利分析中是轉移，不能把整筆稅收當作損失。
items.example: Example 例：CS=120,PS=80,revenue=50. Total post-tax surplus=250. 三者相加。
items.question: After tax CS=40,PS=30,revenue=20. Total surplus? 稅後總剩餘？

items.objective: Identify deadweight loss (DWL) as the lost gains from trades no longer made. For linear curves and an interior equilibrium, calculate `DWL = ½ × tax per unit × (Q before − Q after)`.
items.title: Calculating DWL / 計算無謂損失
items.en: DWL is the lost surplus from trades prevented by the tax. With linear supply and demand and an interior solution, it is the triangle with height t and base Q0−Qt.
items.zh: 無謂損失來自稅令原本互利的交易消失。線性供需內部解下，三角形高為 t，底為減少的交易量。
items.example: Example 例：t=30, Q0=200, Qt=180. DWL=½×30×20=300. 單位稅乘減量再除二。
items.question: t=4, Q0=100, Qt=80. DWL? 無謂損失？

items.objective: Explain that a tax may reduce consumer and producer surplus by more than the government collects; the difference is DWL.
items.title: Lost surplus versus tax receipts / 剩餘損失與稅收
items.en: The reduction in CS plus PS equals government revenue plus DWL in the standard model. Revenue is transferred to government; DWL is the remaining loss in total surplus.
items.zh: CS 與 PS 的總減少等於政府收入加 DWL。稅收只是轉到政府，超出稅收的損失才使總剩餘下降。
items.example: Example 例：Buyers and sellers jointly lose 500; government receives 350. DWL=500−350=150. 無謂損失為一百五十。
items.question: CS+PS falls by 120 and tax revenue is 90. DWL? 私人剩餘跌一百二十、稅收九十？
items.why: 120−90=30 is the part not recovered as government revenue.

items.objective: Compare a tax's effects when demand or supply is more elastic, holding the tax and relevant initial conditions fixed. A larger quantity response creates a larger DWL.
items.title: Elasticity and DWL / 彈性與無謂損失
items.en: Holding the tax and relevant initial conditions fixed, more elastic supply or demand generally causes a larger quantity contraction. A wider base under the same wedge creates greater DWL.
items.zh: 單位稅與相關初始條件相同時，供給或需求更有彈性通常令數量減更多；同一高度下三角形底更大，DWL 更大。
items.example: Example 例：With t=10, a 5-unit fall gives DWL=25; a 15-unit fall gives DWL=75. 同稅而減量不同。
items.question: Same unit tax: market A loses 2 units, B loses 8. Which has larger linear-model DWL? 哪個 DWL 較大？
options: Neither can have DWL / 均無損失
A
B
Equal / 相同
items.why: The wedge height is equal, but B's lost-quantity base is larger.

items.objective: Recognize that a tax on a perfectly inelastic side can raise revenue with zero DWL in this model; understand that zero revenue does not by itself establish zero DWL.
items.title: Zero DWL or zero revenue / 零損失與零稅收
items.en: Perfectly inelastic demand or supply can keep quantity unchanged despite a tax, yielding revenue with zero DWL. Conversely, a prohibitive tax can eliminate trade and raise zero revenue while destroying gains from the original trades.
items.zh: 完全無彈性的一方可令量不變，有稅收但無 DWL。相反，禁止性高稅可把交易降至零，無收入卻失去原本交易收益。
items.example: Example 例：A fixed 100 units still trade under a $2 tax: revenue=200 and DWL=0. If a different high tax prevents all beneficial trade, revenue=0 with positive DWL.
items.question: Can a tax raise zero revenue yet create positive DWL? 稅可無收入但有正 DWL？
options: No, revenue and DWL are identical / 不可，兩者相同
Only if quantity rises / 只在量升
Only with a subsidy / 只限補貼
Yes, if it eliminates beneficial trade / 可，若阻止互利交易
items.why: Zero tax receipts do not mean no lost trading opportunities.

items.objective: Assess whether buyer spending or seller revenue rises or falls after a tax using the demand and supply conditions; a lower seller price and lower quantity reduce seller receipts for ordinary positive prices.
items.title: Buyer spending and seller receipts / 買方支出與賣方淨收
items.en: After a normal unit tax, Ps and Qt both fall, so seller net receipts fall for positive prices. Buyer spending can rise or fall because Pb rises while Q falls; use demand responsiveness or calculate the products.
items.zh: 一般單位稅後賣方淨價及數量皆降，正價格下淨收入下降。買方價升而量跌，支出可升可跌，要看彈性或直接計算。
items.example: Example 例：Before tax P=10,Q=100, spending=1,000. After Pb=12,Q=90, spending=1,080 even though CS falls. 支出增加不代表福利增加。
items.question: Buyer price rises and quantity falls after tax. Buyer spending is always lower? 買方支出必下降嗎？
options: No; it depends on responses / 否，視反應而定
It must be zero / 必零
It equals PS / 等於 PS
Yes / 必下降
items.why: Pb×Q combines opposite effects, so either direction is possible.

items.objective: Trace how an increasing unit tax affects quantity, revenue and DWL; interpret the Laffer curve and recognize that tax revenue need not always increase when the tax rate rises.
items.title: Tax size and the Laffer curve / 稅額與拉弗曲線
items.en: A larger tax generally lowers quantity and raises DWL. Tax revenue equals t×Q(t), so the higher rate can eventually be outweighed by fewer transactions. With linear curves and interior trade, DWL grows quadratically in t.
items.zh: 加稅通常減少交易並增加 DWL；收入為 t×Q(t)，稅更高時數量收縮可能抵消稅額增加。線性內部解下 DWL 隨 t 的平方增加。
items.example: Example 例：If Q(t)=100−t, revenue=t(100−t); t=20 yields 1,600, t=50 yields 2,500, t=80 yields 1,600. 稅額太高可能少收。
items.question: For Q(t)=100−t, which tax maximizes revenue? 哪個稅額收入最高？
items.why: The revenue parabola peaks at t=50. This is not a claim that maximum revenue maximizes welfare.

items.objective: Compare short- and long-run effects when elasticities change. The optional elasticity/Laffer discussion is identified on slide 24.
items.title: Time horizon and taxes / 時間範圍與稅
items.en: Longer-run demand or supply may be more elastic as buyers switch technologies and sellers adjust capacity. With comparable initial conditions and the same tax, the larger long-run quantity response tends to raise DWL and reduce the taxed quantity. The slide-24 elasticity/Laffer extension is optional.
items.zh: 長期可換技術或調產能，供需常更有彈性。同稅及可比較初始條件下，長期減量可能更大、DWL 更高。第 24 張的拉弗延伸標作 optional。
items.example: Example 例：Heating-oil users cannot replace boilers immediately, but may switch fuels over several years. 長期避稅方式更多。
items.question: If the same tax causes a larger quantity reduction in year 5, DWL is generally? 同稅第五年減量更大？
options: Necessarily zero / 必零
Equal to revenue / 等於稅收
Larger / 更大
Smaller / 更小
items.why: The lost-quantity triangle has a larger base.

items.objective: Analyze a per-unit subsidy: `Ps − Pb = subsidy`; quantity typically rises, buyers pay less, sellers receive more, and government expenditure is subsidy times quantity.
items.title: Subsidy equilibrium / 補貼均衡
items.en: A unit subsidy creates Ps−Pb=s. Sellers receive more than buyers pay; supply and demand meet at those separate effective prices. In the ordinary competitive model, quantity rises and government spends s×Qsub.
items.zh: 補貼令 Ps 比 Pb 高 s。用兩個有效價格聯立供需；一般競爭模型下交易量增加，政府支出為 s 乘補貼後交易量。
items.example: Example 例：Qs=Ps,Qd=100−Pb,s=20. Ps=Pb+20 gives Pb=40,Ps=60,Q=60; government spends 1,200.
items.question: Subsidy per unit=3, traded quantity=50. Government spending? 政府支出？
items.why: 3×50=150. Use the subsidized quantity.

items.objective: Calculate subsidy welfare as `CS + PS − government spending`; identify the potential DWL from units whose production cost exceeds buyers' valuation in the standard competitive model.
items.title: Subsidy welfare / 補貼福利
items.en: Subtract government spending from CS+PS. Without external benefits or another relevant distortion, the subsidy induces units whose marginal cost exceeds willingness to pay, causing DWL from overproduction.
items.zh: 總剩餘為 CS+PS 減政府支出。沒有外部效益等因素時，補貼誘使部分成本高於願付價的交易，造成過量生產損失。
items.example: Example 例：CS=80,PS=70,government spending=60. Total surplus=90. If original surplus was 100, DWL=10.
items.question: CS=60,PS=50,subsidy spending=30. Total surplus? 總剩餘？
items.why: 60+50−30=80; spending is a cost in this calculation.

items.objective: Compare a subsidy and a binding price ceiling in terms of price, quantity, shortage and government spending; allow for market failures or other stated assumptions when evaluating policy.
items.title: Subsidy versus ceiling / 補貼與價格上限
items.en: A binding ceiling lowers the allowed price but restricts trade through shortage. A subsidy can lower buyer price while raising seller receipts and quantity, at a fiscal cost. Evaluate welfare using the stated externalities, allocation and government budget.
items.zh: 上限降低合法價格但造成短缺；補貼可同時降低買方價、提高賣方淨收及交易量，但要政府支出。政策評價取決於外部性、配給與財政假設。
items.example: Example 例：Rent ceiling discourages supply; a per-unit housing subsidy can encourage more supply while lowering tenant price. It requires funding. 租客便宜但兩種政策供給誘因不同。
items.question: Which typically requires direct government spending per unit traded? 何者通常每交易一單位需政府付款？
options: Binding ceiling alone / 單純價格上限
Per-unit subsidy / 每單位補貼
Nonbinding floor alone / 無約束下限
Removing a ceiling / 取消上限
items.why: The subsidy pays s for every traded unit; a ceiling itself does not.

sources: Ch 8 slides, especially 2–15, 21–24 and 30–32; `Chapter 6&8.pdf`, Ch 8 questions 7, 8 and 10; `Self-Practice_Chapter 8.pdf`.

items.objective: Calculate total revenue `TR = P × Q`; distinguish explicit costs from implicit opportunity costs, including forgone wages and interest on the owner's funds.
items.title: Revenue and opportunity costs / 收入與機會成本
items.en: TR equals price times quantity. Explicit costs require monetary payments; implicit costs are forgone alternatives for owned resources, such as the owner's wage or interest income. Economic costs include both.
items.zh: 總收入為 P×Q。顯性成本需付款；隱性成本是自有資源放棄的其他收益，例如老闆工資及資金利息。經濟成本包含兩者。
items.example: Example 例：Sell 100 items at $5: TR=500. Rent $100 is explicit; forgone owner wages $150 are implicit. 成本性質取決於有否付款。
items.question: Owner invests savings that could earn $200 interest. This forgone interest is? 放棄利息屬什麼？
options: No economic cost / 無經濟成本
Necessarily a cash expense / 必現金支出
Implicit cost / 隱性成本
Sales revenue / 銷售收入
items.why: Using owned funds sacrifices their next-best return.

items.objective: Calculate accounting profit as revenue minus explicit costs and economic profit as revenue minus both explicit and implicit costs. Interpret zero economic profit as covering all opportunity costs.
items.title: Accounting and economic profit / 會計與經濟利潤
items.en: Accounting profit subtracts explicit costs from revenue. Economic profit also subtracts implicit costs. Zero economic profit covers all opportunity costs, including the owner's normal return.
items.zh: 會計利潤扣顯性成本；經濟利潤再扣隱性成本。零經濟利潤已補償老闆等自有資源的機會成本。
items.example: Example 例：TR=1,000, explicit=600, implicit=300. Accounting profit=400, economic profit=100. 兩種利潤相差隱性成本。
items.question: TR=500, explicit=300, implicit=200. Economic profit? 經濟利潤？
items.why: 500−300−200=0, although accounting profit is 200.

items.objective: Apply marginal decisions using the change in **total** cost, including when average cost changes between output levels; average cost itself is not the cost of one extra unit.
items.title: Marginal cost from total cost / 從總成本求邊際成本
items.en: First convert average costs back to total costs when necessary, then take ΔTC/ΔQ. The extra unit's cost can be much larger than either the average cost or the change in average cost.
items.zh: 先把平均成本乘產量還原總成本，再用 ΔTC/ΔQ。額外單位成本可遠高於平均成本或平均成本增幅。
items.example: Example 例：Q=600,ATC=300 gives TC=180,000; Q=601,ATC=301 gives TC=180,901. The extra unit costs 901.
items.question: Q=10,ATC=5; Q=11,ATC=6. MC of unit 11? 第十一件 MC？
items.why: 11×6−10×5=16. Compare an extra order's revenue with 16.

items.objective: Calculate marginal product `MP = Δoutput / Δinput` from a production table; recognize increasing and diminishing marginal product and explain the shape of the production function.
items.title: Marginal product / 邊際產量
items.en: MP is the change in output divided by the change in an input. It can initially rise with specialization and later fall as workers share fixed equipment. A production function becomes flatter when marginal product diminishes.
items.zh: 邊際產量為產量變化除投入變化。分工可能先提高 MP，但工人共享固定設備後 MP 可遞減；生產函數隨之變平。
items.example: Example 例：Output with 0,1,2,3 workers is 0,10,25,35. MPs are 10,15,10: first rising, then diminishing.
items.question: Output rises from 30 to 42 when labor rises from 3 to 4. MP? 邊際產量多少？

items.objective: Explain, with a fixed input price and other conditions held constant, why diminishing marginal product tends to raise marginal cost. Relate the shape of the production function to the total-cost curve.
items.title: Marginal product and cost / 邊際產量與成本
items.en: With a fixed wage w and labor as the changing input, marginal cost is approximately w/MP. Lower marginal product means more labor per extra unit, raising MC and making total cost steeper as output expands.
items.zh: 工資 w 固定、只調勞工時，MC 約為 w/MP。MP 下降使每件需要更多勞工，MC 上升，總成本曲線變陡。
items.example: Example 例：A $100 worker adds 20 units, costing $5 per extra unit; if the next adds 10, incremental cost becomes $10 per unit. 邊際產量減半，單位額外成本加倍。
items.question: Wage=60 and MP=12. MC? 邊際成本？

items.objective: Identify fixed cost `FC`, variable cost `VC`, and total cost `TC = FC + VC`; recover any missing value in a cost table.
items.title: Fixed, variable and total cost / 固定、可變與總成本
items.en: Fixed cost does not vary with current output in the relevant short run. Variable cost does; TC=FC+VC. At zero output, VC is zero in the standard schedules, so TC(0) identifies FC.
items.zh: 固定成本在相關短期不隨產量改變，可變成本則會。TC=FC+VC；標準表中零產量的 VC=0，因此 TC(0)=FC。
items.example: Example 例：TC at zero is 30. At Q=5, TC=80, so FC=30 and VC=50.
items.question: FC=40 and TC=110. VC? 可變成本？

items.objective: Calculate `AFC = FC/Q`, `AVC = VC/Q`, `ATC = TC/Q = AFC + AVC`, and `MC = ΔTC/ΔQ = ΔVC/ΔQ` when fixed cost does not change. Average costs require `Q > 0`.
items.title: Average and marginal formulas / 平均與邊際公式
items.en: AFC=FC/Q, AVC=VC/Q, ATC=TC/Q=AFC+AVC. MC=ΔTC/ΔQ=ΔVC/ΔQ when FC stays fixed. Average costs are undefined at zero quantity.
items.zh: 平均成本以各項總成本除產量，ATC=AFC+AVC。FC 不變時，MC 也可由 VC 的變化計算。Q=0 時不能計平均成本。
items.example: Example 例：At Q=4,FC=20,VC=28: AFC=5,AVC=7,ATC=12. If Q=5 has TC=60, MC=(60−48)/1=12.
items.question: FC=12,VC=18,Q=3. ATC? 平均總成本？

items.objective: Read and draw the typical curves: AFC falls with output; MC crosses AVC and ATC at their minima; MC below an average pulls it down and MC above it pulls it up.
items.title: Cost curve relationships / 成本線關係
items.en: AFC falls as a fixed sum is spread across output. When MC is below an average it pulls that average down; above it, the average rises. Thus MC crosses AVC and ATC at their respective minima for smooth typical curves.
items.zh: 固定成本分攤更多產量令 AFC 下降；MC 低於平均值會拉低平均，高於平均值會拉高平均。因此 MC 在 AVC、ATC 各自最低點相交。
items.example: Example 例：Current ATC=10; the next unit costs 6. Adding a below-average unit lowers ATC. 下一件較便宜會拉低平均。
items.question: At a given output MC<ATC. What is ATC doing locally? 平均總成本如何變？
options: Undefined / 未定義
Falling / 下降
Rising / 上升
Always at minimum / 必在最低點
items.why: A below-average marginal unit pulls the average down.

items.objective: Identify efficient scale as the output minimizing ATC; calculate it from a cost schedule or graph.
items.title: Efficient scale / 有效率規模
items.en: Efficient scale is the output minimizing ATC. Read the lowest ATC point or compare ATC across a schedule. It is distinct from maximum output and from the minimum AVC shutdown threshold.
items.zh: 有效率規模是 ATC 最低的產量，可由圖最低點或表格比較找出。它與最大產量及 AVC 最低點不同。
items.example: Example 例：ATC at Q=1,2,3,4 is 12,8,7,8. Efficient scale is Q=3. 第三單位產量平均成本最低。
items.question: ATC values at Q=2,3,4 are 9,6,7. Efficient scale among these choices? 有效率規模？
items.why: The minimum listed ATC is 6 at Q=3.

items.objective: Predict which cost curves change with a fixed lump-sum tax versus a per-unit production tax: the former changes FC, AFC and ATC; the latter changes VC, AVC, ATC and MC.
items.title: Lump-sum versus unit tax / 固定總額稅與單位稅
items.en: A fixed lump-sum tax increases FC, AFC and ATC but leaves VC, AVC and MC unchanged. A per-unit tax adds to VC and raises AVC, ATC and MC, leaving FC and AFC unchanged.
items.zh: 固定總額稅增加 FC、AFC、ATC，不改 VC、AVC、MC；每件稅增加 VC、AVC、ATC、MC，不改 FC、AFC。
items.example: Example 例：A $100 firm tax adds 100/Q to ATC. A $2 output tax adds $2 to AVC,ATC and MC. 前者隨產量分攤，後者每件相同。
items.question: Which curve stays unchanged after a fixed lump-sum tax? 固定總額稅後何線不變？
options: Total fixed cost
ATC
AFC
MC
items.why: The tax does not alter the extra cost of another unit.

items.objective: Distinguish fixed inputs in the short run from the ability to vary all inputs and plant scale in the long run.
items.title: Short run and long run / 短期與長期
items.en: In the short run, some inputs or plant scale are fixed. In the long run, all inputs can be adjusted, including entry, exit and plant size. The relevant horizon depends on how long adjustments take, not a universal number of months.
items.zh: 短期有部分投入或規模固定；長期可改全部投入，包括廠房和退出。長短期由調整所需時間決定，沒有通用月份界線。
items.example: Example 例：A bakery can hire overtime this week but needs months to install a larger oven. The oven is fixed in the short run.
items.question: Which is possible in the long run? 長期可以怎樣？
options: Adjust plant size / 調整廠房規模
Only change labor / 只調勞工
No entry or exit / 不可進出
All costs stay fixed / 所有成本固定
items.why: All inputs become adjustable over the long-run horizon.

items.objective: Identify economies of scale, constant returns to scale and diseconomies of scale from how long-run average total cost changes with output; explain specialization and coordination as possible reasons.
items.title: Scale economies / 規模經濟
items.en: Economies of scale mean LRATC falls as output grows, often through specialization. Constant returns to scale mean LRATC is unchanged; diseconomies mean it rises, possibly because coordination becomes harder. Distinguish this from diminishing MP with fixed inputs.
items.zh: 規模經濟是長期 ATC 隨產量下降；不變規模報酬是 ATC 持平；規模不經濟是 ATC 上升，可能來自協調困難。這與固定投入下 MP 遞減不同。
items.example: Example 例：Doubling all inputs doubles output: unchanged cost per unit. If coordination makes costs rise faster than output, LRATC rises.
items.question: Output expands and LRATC falls. What is present? 產量增加、長期平均成本下降？
options: A fixed short-run input by definition / 定義上固定投入
Economies of scale / 規模經濟
Diseconomies of scale / 規模不經濟
Zero marginal cost necessarily / MC 必零
items.why: Falling LRATC is the definition of economies of scale.

items.objective: Identify a competitive market's assumptions: many buyers and sellers, identical products and price-taking behavior; understand free entry and exit as the long-run model assumption.
items.title: Competitive assumptions / 競爭市場假設
items.en: Many buyers and sellers trade identical products, so an individual firm takes the market price as given. Free entry and exit is a long-run assumption that permits industry adjustment when profits change.
items.zh: 許多買賣雙方交易同質產品，個別企業無法自行影響市價。自由進出是長期假設，使利潤吸引進入或虧損引致退出。
items.example: Example 例：One small wheat farmer cannot raise the market wheat price by choosing a personal price. 新企業能進入時，長期正利潤會吸引供給。
items.question: A price-taking firm faces which demand for its output? 價格接受者面對的個別需求？
options: Vertical at zero / 零量垂直線
An upward labor supply curve / 勞工供給線
Horizontal at market price / 市價水平線
The entire downward market demand / 整體市場需求
items.why: It can sell relevant quantities at the given market price; individual and market demand differ.

items.objective: Calculate `TR = P × Q`, `AR = TR/Q`, and `MR = ΔTR/ΔQ`. For a price-taking firm, `P = AR = MR`.
items.title: TR, AR and MR / 總、平均及邊際收入
items.en: TR=Pq, AR=TR/q, and MR=ΔTR/Δq. For a price taker selling every unit at unchanged P, AR and MR both equal P. Market revenue need not have this property if market price changes with total quantity.
items.zh: TR=Pq，AR=TR/q，MR=ΔTR/Δq。個別價格接受企業每件以同價出售，故 P=AR=MR；不可直接套到會影響價格的整體市場。
items.example: Example 例：P=$8. Selling 3 units gives TR=24; selling 4 gives TR=32, so MR=8 and AR=8.
items.question: A competitive firm sells 5 units at $6 each. AR and MR? AR 及 MR？
options: AR=30,MR=6
AR=6,MR=30
AR=5,MR=6
AR=6,MR=6
items.why: Revenue per unit and extra-unit revenue both equal price.

items.objective: Find the profit-maximizing output by comparing total profit across feasible quantities or producing up to the point where marginal revenue equals marginal cost on the relevant rising MC segment. With discrete units, compare the extra revenue and extra cost of each unit.
items.title: Choosing output / 選擇產量
items.en: Compare total profit across feasible quantities, including zero. For a smooth standard cost curve and a firm that operates, select the rising MC intersection with MR. With discrete units, expand while the added revenue covers the added cost, checking ties and nonstandard cost patterns.
items.zh: 比較各可行產量及零產量的總利潤。一般平滑成本線營運時取上升 MC 與 MR 交點；離散單位須比較每件額外收益成本並留意特殊成本。
items.example: Example 例：P=10, successive MCs=4,7,12. The first two units add profit; the third reduces it. Choose q=2 if operating beats shutdown.
items.question: P=9; MCs of three units are 3,8,11. Best operating output? 最佳營運產量？
options: 0 solely because MC rises / MC 上升所以零
items.why: Unit 2 adds 9−8=1; unit 3 adds 9−11=−2.

items.objective: Check the shutdown choice as well as candidate outputs: an `MR = MC` intersection alone does not establish the global profit maximum, especially with multiple intersections or discrete output.
items.title: Checking the global choice / 檢查整體最佳選擇
items.en: MR=MC alone is only a candidate condition. Compare other intersections, feasible discrete quantities and shutdown. A falling-MC intersection can be a profit minimum, and an operating optimum can still lose more than producing zero.
items.zh: MR=MC 只提供候選點；還要比較其他交點、離散產量及停產。下降 MC 的交點可能是利潤最低，營運解也可能不及零產量。
items.example: Example 例：P=5; TC(0)=10,TC(1)=15,TC(2)=16. Unit 1 has MR=MC=5, but profits at q=0,1,2 are −10,−10,−6. q=2 is better.
items.question: An MR=MC point exists but its profit is −80; shutdown loses only 50. Choose? 交點虧八十，停產虧五十？
options: Operate at the intersection / 在交點營運
Shut down / 停產
Increase output without checking / 不檢查就增產
Exit must be immediate / 必立即退出
items.why: Compare total profit: −50 exceeds −80.

items.objective: Calculate profit or loss as `TR − TC = (P − ATC) × Q`; identify the profit or loss rectangle on a graph.
items.title: Profit and loss rectangle / 利潤與虧損面積
items.en: Profit=TR−TC=(P−ATC)q, with ATC evaluated at the chosen output. On a graph, the height is P−ATC and the width is q. A negative height means loss.
items.zh: 利潤=(P−ATC)q，ATC 要在所選產量讀取。圖中長方形高為價與 ATC 差，闊為 q；價低於 ATC 就是虧損。
items.example: Example 例：P=12,ATC=9,q=20. Profit=(12−9)×20=60. 每件賺三元、二十件賺六十。
items.question: P=7,ATC=10,q=5. Profit? 利潤？

items.objective: Apply the short-run shutdown rule: shut down when `P < AVC` at the best operating quantity, or equivalently `TR < VC`; fixed costs remain payable. At equality, the firm is indifferent under the model.
items.title: Shutdown rule / 停產法則
items.en: In the short run, fixed costs remain payable. Shut down if the best operating revenue cannot cover variable cost: TR<VC, or P<AVC at that candidate output. At the threshold, operating and shutdown can give equal profit.
items.zh: 短期停產仍要付固定成本。最佳營運方案若 TR<VC，等同該產量 P<AVC，就應停產；臨界相等時兩者無差異。
items.example: Example 例：TR=80,VC=100,FC=50. Operating loses 70; shutdown loses 50. Stop production for the period.
items.question: P=4,AVC=5 at the best operating candidate. Short-run decision? 最佳候選產量下價四、AVC 五？
options: Operate because revenue is positive / 收入正就營運
Ignore variable cost / 忽略 VC
Enter more markets automatically / 自動進入更多市場
Shut down / 停產
items.why: Revenue fails to cover avoidable variable costs.

items.objective: Distinguish operating at a loss from shutting down: a firm may continue if revenue covers variable costs and contributes toward fixed costs.
items.title: Operating at a loss / 虧損下營運
items.en: A loss does not by itself imply shutdown. If revenue covers VC and some FC, operating reduces the loss compared with paying all FC without production. Compare the two profit levels explicitly.
items.zh: 虧損本身不足以判斷停產。收入涵蓋 VC 並支付部分 FC 時，營運虧損較少；把兩個方案利潤直接比較最清楚。
items.example: Example 例：TR=150,VC=100,FC=100. Operate: profit=−50. Shutdown: profit=−100. Continue this period.
items.question: TR=90,VC=70,FC=40. Operating profit versus shutdown? 營運和停產利潤？
options: −20 versus −40 / 營運較好
−40 versus −20 / 停產較好
+20 versus 0 / 營運賺二十
−90 versus −70 / 均按收入損失
items.why: Operating loss=90−70−40=−20; shutdown pays FC=40.

items.objective: Apply the long-run exit rule `P < ATC`, and entry incentive when economic profit is positive; at equality, the firm earns zero economic profit.
items.title: Long-run entry and exit / 長期進入與退出
items.en: With all costs avoidable in the long run, persistent P<ATC creates an exit incentive. Positive economic profit attracts entry where entry is free. At P=ATC, normal opportunity costs are covered and economic profit is zero.
items.zh: 長期全部成本可調整，持續 P<ATC 會引致退出；自由進入下正經濟利潤吸引新企業。P=ATC 已涵蓋正常機會成本。
items.example: Example 例：P=8 and minimum sustainable ATC=10: remaining indefinitely gives a negative economic return, encouraging exit.
items.question: In the long run P>ATC with free entry. Expected response? 長期價高於 ATC，自由進入？
options: Shutdown because profit is positive / 正利潤所以停產
Entry / 進入
Exit / 退出
No incentive to enter / 無進入誘因
items.why: Positive economic profit attracts entrants under the model.

items.objective: Identify the firm's short-run supply as the relevant rising part of MC at or above AVC, with zero output below the shutdown threshold; identify its long-run supply relative to ATC.
items.title: Firm supply thresholds / 企業供給門檻
items.en: Short-run supply follows the rising MC branch above minimum AVC; lower prices imply zero output. The textbook long-run supply rule uses rising MC at or above minimum ATC when all costs are avoidable. At thresholds, indifference can occur.
items.zh: 短期供給取最低 AVC 以上的上升 MC，低於門檻供給為零。課本長期供給以最低 ATC 為門檻；門檻處可無差異。
items.example: Example 例：Minimum AVC=3 and minimum ATC=5. At P=4, the firm may operate in the short run yet prefer exit in the long run.
items.question: Price is below minimum AVC. Short-run supply? 價低於最低 AVC，短期供給？
options: Efficient-scale output / 有效率規模
A negative quantity / 負數產量
Zero / 零
The full MC curve / 全條 MC
items.why: Every positive operating option fails to cover variable cost.

items.objective: Sum individual quantities supplied horizontally to find market supply with a fixed number of firms. Given market demand and the number of identical firms, solve for the short-run market price, market quantity, firm output and profit.
items.title: Market equilibrium with N firms / N 家企業的市場均衡
items.en: Sum each firm's q(P) horizontally. With identical firms, market supply is Nq(P). Equate this to market demand, solve P, then compute q and profit using the firm's own costs.
items.zh: 先以 Nq(P) 得市場供給，再與市場需求相等求價。個別產量與利潤必須用企業自己的成本計算。
items.example: Example 例：TC=50+q²/2,MC=q, N=9; Qd=120−P. Each q=P, so 9P=120−P gives P=12,Q=108,q=12; profit=144−122=22.
items.question: Four identical firms each supply q=P. Demand Qd=100−P. Market price? 四家各供 q=P，市場價？
items.why: 4P=100−P gives P=20 and market Q=80.

items.objective: Trace how positive profit induces entry and shifts market supply right, while losses induce exit and shift supply left, under free entry and exit.
items.title: Entry and supply adjustment / 進入與供給調整
items.en: Positive profit induces entry, shifting market supply right and lowering price; losses induce exit, shifting supply left and raising price, holding demand and relevant costs fixed. Adjustment continues until entry or exit incentives disappear.
items.zh: 需求及相關成本不變下，正利潤吸引進入使市場供給右移、價跌；虧損引致退出使供給左移、價升，直到進出誘因消失。
items.example: Example 例：A profitable wheat industry attracts farmers. Greater market supply reduces price and each firm's economic profit. 更多企業分攤市場需求。
items.question: Firms incur persistent losses and exit. Market supply moves? 虧損退出後市場供給？
options: Left / 左移
Right / 右移
Only demand moves / 只需求移動
Quantity axis changes units / 數量軸單位改變
items.why: Fewer firms supply less at a given price.

items.objective: In the standard identical-firm, free-entry long-run equilibrium, identify `P = MR = MC = minimum ATC`, zero economic profit, and production at efficient scale. Determine market quantity and number of firms from demand and output per firm.
items.title: Long-run equilibrium and firm count / 長期均衡與企業數
items.en: For identical firms with free entry and constant input costs, long-run equilibrium has P=MC=min ATC and zero economic profit. Obtain market Q from demand at that price, then divide by efficient-scale q to find N.
items.zh: 相同企業、自由進出及投入成本不變時，長期 P=MC=最低 ATC，經濟利潤為零。市需求求 Q，再除個別有效率產量得企業數。
items.example: Example 例：TC=50+q²/2 gives ATC=50/q+q/2. Its minimum is at q=10 with ATC=MC=10. Qd=120−P gives Q=110, so N=11.
items.question: Long-run P=8, market Q=160, each firm q=10. Number of firms? 企業數？

items.objective: Explain how a demand change affects price and profits in the short run, then entry or exit and the long-run outcome. Understand why long-run industry supply can be horizontal under identical constant-cost conditions and upward sloping if input costs rise or firms differ.
items.title: Demand changes across horizons / 需求變化的短長期
items.en: A demand increase raises price and operating output in the short run with a fixed number of firms. Profits then attract entry. With identical constant-cost firms, long-run price returns to minimum ATC while market quantity and firm count rise. Limited inputs or differing firm costs can make LR supply upward sloping.
items.zh: 需求增加先令短期價、每家產量及利潤升；長期進入擴大供給。相同固定成本行業長期價回最低 ATC，總量及企業數增加；投入稀缺或成本不同可令長期供給向上。
items.example: Example 例：Long-run price is 10 and firm q=10. Demand expansion raises total long-run Q from 100 to 140, increasing firm count from 10 to 14.
items.question: Constant-cost industry: demand permanently rises. Long-run price? 固定成本行業需求永久增加，長期價？
options: Falls to zero necessarily / 必跌零
Equals total market quantity / 等於市場總量
Returns to minimum ATC / 回到最低 ATC
Stays above ATC forever / 永遠高於 ATC
items.why: Entry expands supply until economic profit is driven to zero.

items.objective: Analyze a change in an input price or a firm's technology: shift the appropriate cost curves, determine short-run profits, and trace potential long-run industry adjustment. Consider whether a patented innovation can be copied when assessing entry or competition.
items.title: Input costs, technology and patents / 投入成本、技術與專利
items.en: An input-price increase raises relevant variable costs and MC, shifting market supply left. Technology can lower costs; trace the short-run price and profits before deciding entry or exit. A patent can keep an innovator's advantage from being copied until it expires.
items.zh: 投入價升提高相關 VC、MC，令市場供給左移。技術進步可降成本；先求短期價與利潤再判斷進出。專利可暫時阻止其他企業複製優勢。
items.example: Example 例：One firm's patented process lowers its cost while market price barely changes. It earns extra profit; after expiry, broad adoption can lower market price. 專利到期後優勢可能擴散。
items.question: A patented cost reduction is available only to one small firm. Its immediate profit at an unchanged price? 價不變、單一小企業專利降成本？
options: Falls / 下降
Must be zero / 必零
Cannot differ from rivals / 必與對手相同
Rises / 上升
items.why: Lower costs at a given price raise profit; entry cannot immediately copy protected technology.

items.objective: Label units and the relevant price: market price, buyer price, seller's net price, wage received or employer cost.
items.title: Identify the price and units / 確認價格與單位
items.en: Write what each price measures before calculating: buyer payment, seller net receipt, worker wage or employer total cost. A unit tax has currency per unit; government revenue has currency.
items.zh: 先標出價格身份及單位：買方付款、賣方淨收、工人淨工資或企業勞工成本。單位稅為每件金額，政府收入則為總金額。
items.example: Example 例：Pb=12,Ps=9,Q=100. The unit wedge is $3 per unit; total revenue is $300. 每件三元與總三百元不同。
items.question: Employer cost=25, worker wage=20, hours=10. Total payroll tax? 工資稅總額？

items.objective: Check whether a question asks for a **change in a curve** or a **movement along** it, and whether other determinants are held constant.
items.title: Check curve versus movement / 檢查移線或沿線
items.en: Identify the market and the changed determinant. Own price changes quantity along a curve; another determinant can move the entire curve. Keep all stated “other things equal” assumptions in place.
items.zh: 先找市場及變動因素；自身價格改變沿線，其他決定因素改變可移線。題目指定其他不變的條件要保留。
items.example: Example 例：A rise in coffee price moves along coffee demand but can shift tea demand. 同一事件對不同市場的曲線影響不同。
items.question: A good's production cost falls. Which curve shifts in its market? 生產成本下降？
options: The PPF must vanish / PPF 消失
Supply / 供給
Demand solely because cost fell / 成本降直接需求移
Neither; only its own price changed / 只是自身價變
items.why: Cost is a supply determinant, not an own-price movement.

items.objective: Distinguish total, average and marginal values; use the marginal value for an additional-unit decision.
items.title: Total, average or marginal / 總、平均或邊際
items.en: A total is an accumulated amount; an average divides a total by quantity; a marginal value measures the change from an additional unit. Match the measure to the question's decision.
items.zh: 總值是累積金額，平均值為總值除數量，邊際值是多一單位的變化。問是否增加一件，就使用額外收益及額外成本。
items.example: Example 例：TC(4)=40 and TC(5)=47. At q=5, ATC=9.4 but fifth-unit MC=7. 平均與新增成本不同。
items.question: TC rises from 100 to 118 when Q rises from 10 to 12. MC per extra unit over this interval? 每額外單位成本？

items.objective: When a numerical answer depends on a graph, identify the quantity actually traded and any stated assumptions about rationing, taxes or subsidies before calculating areas.
items.title: Traded quantity and graph assumptions / 交易量與圖形假設
items.en: Before measuring areas, establish actual traded quantity and the effective price paid or received. Under controls, the short side limits voluntary trade and allocation assumptions determine who gets the units.
items.zh: 畫面積前先確定售出量及有效價格。管制下自願交易取較小供需量；商品分給誰也會影響福利。
items.example: Example 例：Ceiling gives Qd=80,Qs=50. Use at most 50 traded units for welfare, then state which buyers obtain them. 需求八十不能當作已售八十。
items.question: With Qd=100,Qs=60 under a ceiling and no extra supply, maximum voluntary trades? 最多交易量？
items.why: The 60-unit supply is the short side.

items.objective: For a before-and-after question, distinguish a participant's gain or loss from the change in total surplus and from government revenue or expenditure.
items.title: Private gains versus social welfare / 私人收益與社會福利
items.en: Separate changes in CS, PS and government revenue or spending before adding total surplus. A participant gaining money does not establish a social gain; transfers can change distribution without increasing total value.
items.zh: 分別算 CS、PS 及政府收入或支出，再加總。某方得益不等於社會總收益增加；轉移付款可只改變分配。
items.example: Example 例：After a subsidy CS rises 30, PS rises 20, government spends 60. Total surplus changes by 30+20−60=−10. 私人均得益但總剩餘減十。
items.question: CS rises 10,PS rises 15,government spends 40. Change in total surplus? 總剩餘變化？
